News.title: Woman who killed husband & dismembered his body before dumping remains in bags across city reveals why she did it
News.content:
‘HAD ENOUGH’ Woman who killed husband & dismembered his body before dumping remains in bags across city reveals why she did it

A WIFE has confessed to killing and dismembering her husband before scattering his body parts in bin bags across Sydney.

Nirmeen Noufl, 55, plead guilty to manslaughter and revealed that her 30-year marriage had been riddled with abuse and infidelity.



Nirmeen revealed the grim series of events which lead up to the death of her husband Mahmoud Noufl’s death in May 2023.

She claimed they had a violent argument with Mahmoud, 62, chasing her from room to room before pinning her to the kitchen floor and trying to choke her.



Fearing for her life, she grabbed a nearby tool lying around from the house renovation and stabbed him in the chest.

Two months later Mahmoud was reported missing – and in October 2024 Nirmeen was charged with one count of murder.



She had been due to appear in court for a mammoth 40-day murder trial – but at the 11th-hour Nirmeen plead guilty to manslaughter.

She confessed to killing her husband in their Greenacre home sometime between May 3 and May 4, 2023.

The couple’s more than 30-year marriage had reportedly been turbulent – with multiple counts of alleged violence and infidelity.



Days before his death, Mahmoud had revealed that he was having an affair – and planning to marry his mistress.

Nirmeen initially demanded a divorce – but then resorted to more desperate measures, unable to ignore “the voices in my head”.

A witness had spotted Nirmeen with a cut to her forehead, bleeding lip and a swollen jaw on the night of the killing.

The same witness, who cannot be named, also said they had seen a “large round saw” beneath plastic tarp on the floor of the house.



She later dismembered the body and strew the remains across suburbs in Sydney.

His scattered corpse is yet to be found – making it difficult to establish how he was killed.

Acoording to court docs, Nirmeen told a friend that she “had enough” of being treated “like sh*t”.

“We had a fight and he was laughing at me”, she told a witness who cannot be identified.

“He just treated me like sh*t, spat at me. I had enough.



“I have been trying to ignore the voices in my head.

“I’m sorry and that I regret it, but I genuinely believe it didn’t happen, and I don’t know how I did it.”

Documents suggest that Mahmoud – who held conservative Islamic views – had been “controlling of his wife”.

He refused to divorce her – even after telling her he planned to elope to Egypt with another woman.

The mistress had been sent around £8,000 (550,000 Egyptian pounds) to buy a new home abroad – but two weeks after Mahmoud’s death, she recieved a Facebook message demanding the money back.



Unaware that her lover had been killed, she asked for a voice message from the sender.

The unidentified messenger replied: “You have no shame. You know that this money belongs to my wife Nirmeen. So even if she is the one sending the message, she (has) the right to demand it from you.”

Nirmeen had access to her husband’s Facebook account – but court docs do not confirm whether she was the sender.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

For two months Nirmeen kept up the ruse that her husband was still alive, sending messages from his phone and turning away relatives who tried to visit by saying that he was tired and did not want to see anyone.

She said he “did not want to talk to anyone because he was embarrassed and ashamed about his affair”.

News.title: New hosepipe ban is announced for first time in over 30 years for 1.2million Brits – and it’s coming into force TOMORROW
News.content:
A NEW hosepipe ban is being introduced for over a million Brits for the first time in 36 years.

This is the tenth supplier in England and Wales to introduce restrictions as nearly three-quarters of Brits face drought conditions.

Bristol Water has confirmed that a temporary hosepipe ban will come into force tomorrow to protect the River Severn’s water resources as a result of drought.



This is the first hosepipe ban the supplier has introduced because of drought since 1975 and generally since 1990, with around 1.2million Brits set to be affected.



Richard Stanbrook, director for drinking water services at Bristol Water, said: “Introducing a hosepipe ban is never a decision we take lightly, and we fully appreciate the inconvenience it will cause.”

Large parts of the South West of England will be affected, with the ban covering Bristol, Weston Super Mare, Portishead, Glastonbury and other locations.

Bristol Water has confirmed that the restrictions will be enforced in its supply area from 0.01am on Thursday, August 27.

Under a temporary use ban, customers cannot use a hosepipe, sprinkler, or pressure washer for various activities, such as watering plants or filling up hot tubs.

Anyone caught breaking the rules can face a £1,000 fine, unless an approved exemption or loophole is in place.

The supplier joins around half of the UK’s water companies have introduced hosepipe bans throughout the summer, including Thames Water, Wessex Water and Southern Water.



This follows a summer of prolonged dry conditions and five heatwaves, with drought declared across 70 per cent of England and the entirety of Wales, with Bristol and the South West affected.

During this period, Bristol Water says that half of its water has come from river sources, resulting in a significant impact on the River Severn’s resources.

The South West of England currently has the lowest reservoir capacity in the entire country, according to Defra, as resources continue to be stretched.

Wimbleball reservoir, about an hour’s drive south of Bristol Water’s supply area, is considered to have exceptionally low water levels for this time of year.



If your water supplier is affected, it is important to check their website to find out if your postcode has been impacted by temporary use bans.

Blue Badge holders, and those on the Priority Services Register, are exempt from the rules as well as those who require the use of a hose for a medical purpose.

News.title: Bizarre truth behind the haunting Cat in the Hat ‘serial killer’ terrifying Brit kids… and the even scarier paedo threat
News.content:
“I’M COMING… LOCK YOUR DOORS” reads the sinister caption on a viral TikTok video of someone dressed as Dr Seuss character The Cat in the Hat dancing robotically.

The clip, which racked up a million views, joins a legion of others showing the children’s book favourite in similarly menacing scenarios – and it is leaving UK kids and teens terrified.



Some have claimed an individual in the costume carried out assaults, stalked them while walking home at night and sent “threatening messages” warning of a plan to carry out “violent acts”.

Youngsters in every corner of the country have been terrorised by TikTok footage and photos of the creepy cat.

But it is all a hoax. Artificial intelligence is behind the creepy creations – all made for online clout, followers and money.



In just over a week, the wild speculation about this mythical ‘attacker’ has caused such concern that police in Wexford, Ireland, were forced to share a post debunking the theories and outing the clips and photos as fakes.

They claimed to have received a number of distressing reports of the cat “causing havoc in neighbourhoods and towns across the country”.

A spokesperson added: “To be clear, the Cat in the Hat was not in your driveway while you were out and he is not currently hiding out in [the village of] Curracloe.”

Similarly, South Yorkshire Police had to denounce a fake online account pretending to be them, which wrongly claimed there was “suspicious behaviour” in the Meadowhall area.

The phony post urged homeowners to lock all windows and doors, insisted that extra police patrols had been ordered and said they were taking the incident “seriously”.



An SYP spokesperson encouraged the public not to believe everything they see online and jokingly added: “We can also confirm no recent sightings of his associates Thing One and Thing Two.”

While the claims of a Cat in the Hat killer may seem laughable, teenagers and children around the UK believe and fear it.

Multiple clips showing the eerie lifelike character alongside the locations he will strike in next have spread like wildfire. And, worryingly, some parents are adding fuel to the flames.

In response to Wexford police’s statement, one person claimed: “He was in Coolcotts last night chasing kids with a knife. My daughter showed me the video.”

Another insisted “it’s not AI” because their daughter “saw him in Ashford the night before last”. Hysterical fear has spread among young people.



Ellie, 16, from the Scottish Borderlands, told the BBC: “I was so scared of him when I was little. Now it’s like he’s actually come to life to haunt me.”

Another, Skye, 16, decided to leave a friend’s sleepover at 3am because she was so worried after watching clips of the freaky feline.

“I wanted to go home,” she said.

“When I started walking down my friends’ driveway, I got totally freaked out that the Cat in the Hat was going to jump out. I had to call my mum to pick me up.”

More concerningly, one account observed by Lily, 14, claimed they would be arranging a “meet and greet” for TikTok followers in the woods near Galashields, near Scotland.



Thankfully, she spoke to her mum, who rightly warned her there could be a predator, paedophile or attacker waiting for anyone who attended.

She told Lily: “You are not going to meet anyone in the woods in the middle of the night!”

No police force so far has expressed any concern about a Cat in the Hat ‘attacker’ – but it’s clear from posts seen by The Sun that some people on social media have their concerns.



On an Essex Facebook community group, one person anonymously posted that their younger siblings had received “threatening messages” on Snapchat and TikTok.

They wrote: “This was from a user called the ‘cat in the hat’, messaging them that they will be committing violent acts and to lock their doors and windows as they are ‘coming to Loughton.’”

The individual, whose claims are unverified, said one sibling, who has a learning disability, was “panicking” and they feared the kids would be “scared to leave the house”.

They claimed they had contacted the police and urged parents to ensure their children’s social media accounts had the location feature disabled and to warn kids about the hoax.

One mum in St Helier, Jersey, claimed on a community board that she had seen an individual dressed like the character “running around quite erratically”.



She admitted being uncertain if it was “teenagers messing around” or a genuine threat, before adding: “It really scared my six-year-old.”

Another lady in Mansfield, Nottinghamshire, shared screenshots of an exchange with her daughter where she begged her to lock all windows and doors.

The message read: “There’s a cat in the hat lurking [a]round Mansfield and police have even sent a warning on Facebook… it’s so scary, people are getting chased.”



The hoax comes a decade on from a viral ‘killer clown’ trend, where individuals would dress as clowns and lurk near schools, dark roads and forests to scare people.

Often they would film the reactions of the spooked strangers to upload online. The phenomenon spread from the state of Wisconsin across the US and then to the UK, Europe and Australia.

Other iterations, all attempting to recreate the posts’ viral success, have followed, including someone who dressed as Stephen King’s Pennywise the clown from IT.

Now these hoaxes are more easily spread because AI can create lifelike people and scenarios for videos and photos. It’s easily achievable with a few clicks on a smartphone.

Last year, an AI prank saw a daughter trick her “extremely concerned parent” into believing she was home alone with a homeless man she had taken in.



The mum was so scared that she called Dorset Police, who attended the scene and discovered it was fake. They then urged people to conduct research before calling 999.

It’s likely police forces across the UK are cautious to give oxygen to this new Cat in the Hat attacker hoax and will want to ensure already-stretched police time isn’t wasted.

The trend’s origins are unknown, but one theory pointed to a viral post on X, formerly Twitter, about the original costume from 2003 film The Cat in the Hat being listed for auction.



The furry outfit, which is tipped to sell for £17,500 under this hammer on Wednesday, was labelled “genuine nightmare fuel” and “scary as f***” by commenters.

On the August 8 post, which received 10 million views, one person wrote: “This is a horror movie in the making.”

Another clip that showed someone dressed in the original Cat in the Hat costume was captioned “Help, what do I do?” racked up 15 million views.

Seeing the viral popularity achievable may have inspired people to turn to AI to create their own creepy clips for online clout or to make money.

“An AI image costs seconds to make but ‘buys’ millions of views,” Ruth Azar-Knupffer, Co-Founder at VerifyLabs.AI, tells The Sun.



“The platforms also pay in reach, followers and sometimes in money, for exactly the emotions this material produces.”

In addition to this, Ruth suspects that for some people “frightening teenagers has some kind of pay-off” for them. Others like sharing conspiracies without thinking about the consequences

She believes the public at large needs to have access to deepfake detecting technology to avoid falling for these types of hoaxes again.

She tells us: “The lesson is that the public is unarmed. Verification is currently a service sold to institutions while the people actually being targeted are left to squint at their screens and guess.

“Until everyone has access to a deepfake detector, they will continue to be the victims of other people’s imaginations, however dark those imaginations get.”

News.title: Will the lunar eclipse be visible from my area? UK weather forecast for the Blood Moon – and best time to see it
News.content:
STARGAZERS across the UK are gearing up for a spectacular celestial show this week as a stunning “Blood Moon” takes to the skies.

Those who set their alarms for the early hours of Friday, August 28 will be in for a treat as the UK experiences a partial lunar eclipse – with over 93% of the Moon’s face plunging into the darkest part of Earth’s shadow.



It will look almost identical to a total lunar eclipse, and you can even leave the specialist eyewear at home.

A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth positions itself directly between the Sun and the Moon, stopping sunlight from directly reaching the lunar surface.



During a near total lunar eclipse, the Moon is bathed in a dramatic red, copper-like glow caused by the Earth’s atmosphere – hence the nickname “Blood Moon”.

It’s a sight you won’t want to miss, but to fully appreciate it, you’ll need a decent break in the clouds.

When is the best time to see the lunar eclipse?

The eclipse is an hours-long event, but the action kicks off at 2.23am on Friday, August 28, as Earth’s outer shadow first touches the Moon, causing a subtle dimming.

The partial eclipse officially begins at 3.33am, when a distinct dark “bite” will appear across the lunar disk as it enters the Earth’s main shadow.

The peak of the eclipse will arrive at 5.12am, when maximum coverage will cause the Moon to glow in dramatic reddish-orange hues – the “Blood Moon” effect.

Around 6.15am, the Moon dips below the horizon, wrapping up visibility across the UK.



How to get the best views of the eclipse

Getting a good view of peak eclipse will require some forward planning, due to how low the Moon will be in the sky – roughly eight degrees above the west-southwest horizon.

Your primary goal is securing an unobstructed line of sight.

Seek out high ground like a local hilltop, an open park, or a west-facing coastline to ensure tall buildings, trees, or hills don’t block your view.

While the red glow of the Moon will be bright enough to spot from suburban back gardens, stepping away from light pollution and city streetlights will make the spectacle more vivid.

Unlike the solar eclipse seen earlier this month, you can leave the specialist eyewear in the drawer and look directly at the Moon with the naked eye.



You don’t need to bring any special gear, but if you’re lucky enough to own a pair of binoculars or a camera with a zoom lens, you should be able to get a closer look at the crimson-lit craters.

What is the weather forecast where you live?

Your best-laid eclipse plans may be scuppered if the Great British weather refuses to play ball, and cloud cover is the ultimate threat to skygazers.

The Met Office has issued its latest update, but says that “weather conditions are expected to be challenging for many hoping to see the eclipse.”

If you live in the South or East of England, you may have drawn the lucky ticket, at least to start with.

The Met Office says: “The best initial viewing opportunities are… likely to be across southern and eastern England.



“These areas are expected to remain relatively cloud-free from around 2am, potentially allowing observers to see the opening stages of the eclipse.”

But for many others, the start of the eclipse is going to be hidden behind a blanket of grey.

“At the beginning of the event,” says the Met Office, “cloud is forecast across Cornwall and Devon, Wales, the Midlands, parts of northwest England, and most of Scotland and Northern Ireland.”

But “cloud amounts are also expected to build elsewhere across the UK, meaning conditions may become increasingly unfavourable before the eclipse reaches its maximum at 5.12am.”

There is slightly better news if you live in the North East of England, where “patchier cloud is expected,” meaning you might just get lucky and spot the red Moon peeking through the gaps.



The Blood Moon weather forecast where you live:

Cornwall & Devon: Cloudy from the start of the event, creating generally challenging early viewing conditions.

Cloudy from the start of the event, creating generally challenging early viewing conditions. Midlands & Northwest England: Overcast skies expected early on, with cloud amounts building as the night progresses.

The Met Office says that though “the greatest chance of seeing something is likely to be across southern and eastern England during its earlier stages… there may not be one location offering ideal conditions throughout.”

“Cloud cover can vary over relatively short distances,” it says, “so those planning to watch should check the latest local forecast before setting out.”

News.title: Brits would get £30 tax break if left on hold by HMRC for 30 minutes under Reform plans
News.content:
PAY PER WAIT Brits would get £30 tax break if left on hold by HMRC for 30 minutes under Reform plans

TAXPAYERS would get £30 knocked off their tax bill if they are left hanging on the phone to HMRC for more than 30 minutes under Reform plans.

The payout would be capped at twice a year and only available to people who owe tax.



The party’s Treasury spokesperson Robert Jenrick announced the move at a press conference this morning, saying: “Last year, MPs were accusing HMRC of deliberately degrading its own services to force people onto the website. It’s a disgrace.

“Frankly, it is offensive to working people and I have had enough.



“So, we will give HMRC a big incentive to actually provide proper customer service.

“I’m announcing today that under a Reform government, if you spend more than half an hour waiting for HMRC to answer your call, you will get a £30 credit off your tax bill. If HMRC delay, well, they can repay.

“And to make sure that the staff actually hit their targets, we’ll tie the pay of senior HMRC officials to their customer service performance.”

Callers waited an average of 23 minutes in 2023/24 – compared with just five minutes five years earlier.

Nearly 50,000 calls were reportedly cut off without help after hitting HMRC’s 70-minute limit.

Reform claims taxpayers lost 14 million hours on the phone that year, costing the economy £275million in wasted time.



The party expects the tax credits to cost £70million annually but says the bill would fall if HMRC answered calls faster.

Officials would be ordered to improve services without extra departmental cash, including by letting small firms arrange debt repayments in writing.

At the press conference, Mr Jenrick also pledged to scrap UK privacy rules in favour of a “light-touch” approach to data protection as part of a bid to slash “red tape” for businesses.

News.title: Brits to be told ‘stock up on bottled water & tinned food to prepare for threats including cyber attacks & weather’
News.content:
HOME FRONT Brits to be told ‘stock up on bottled water & tinned food to prepare for threats including cyber attacks & weather’

BRITS are reportedly to be told to stock up on water and tinned food to prepare for threats posed by cyber attacks and weather.

Andy Burnham’s government is understood to be preparing a campaign to warn households how to be ready for severe disruption.



It comes after it was revealed that a cyber attack on a UK energy facility, thought to be linked to Iran, shut down the facility.

Work on a government “war book” is said to have been accelerated after ex-PM Keir Starmer said there could be an attack by Russia against Nato as soon as 2030.



The “war book” is a detailed manual for the defence of the UK from external threats.

Amid the rising tensions, people are believed they will be told to ensure they have emergency supplies like canned food and water on hand.

The Financial Times reports that a focus has been put on national resilience after Russia threatened the UK with “consequences” when British drones were used by Ukraine in long-range strikes.

Seperately, the attack on a UK energy facility, allegedly by Iran, has prompted claims that the country’s infrastructure is vulnerable.

Dieter Helm, professor of economic policy at Oxford university, said the UK’s energy system was “very vulnerable” to cyber attacks.

He added that it was time for ministers to “wake up and smell the coffee.”



Downing Street has insisted that Britain had “One of the most resilient energy systems in the world”, however.

Officials confirmed that Andy Burnham is making preparations for the country to face severe disruption.

Darren Jones, former Cabinet Office minister, announced at the end of Keir Starmer’s premiership that work was being sped-up on “updating the government ‘war book.'”

The manual was last updated in 2004.

A social media campaign is now reportedly being prepared to tell people how to prepare for disruption caused by weather, hostile state action or cyber attacks.



A source told the Financial Times: “There will be practical advice on things you can do to improve domestic resilience, like having some bottled water and tinned food.

“It will be common sense, not scaremongering.”

The Cabinet Office said: “Safeguarding national security is the first priority of any government.

“We’re committed to raising awareness of simple steps households can take to make themselves more resilient, as well as driving forward the Home Defence Programme to build our country’s preparedness for various threats.”

News.title: Buc-ee’s confirms ‘visible’ tattoo ban in strict nationwide policy for all 56 stores
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

NEW STORE POLICY Buc-ee’s confirms ‘visible’ tattoo ban in strict nationwide policy for all 56 stores

ROAD trip stop Buc-ee’s has forbidden their staff from sporting “visible tattoos” in a nationwide ban.

Famed across the US for the squeaky-clean bathrooms, Buc-ee’s has announced that staff at all 56 stores are also not allowed to wear “torn or faded clothing”.



Other dress code decrees include a ban on “unnatural coloured hair, open toe shoes, and body piercings.”

But what they must wear, according to their website, are “tan/khaki/black pants and a clean, professional, solid red shirt with a collar.”



“In cooler weather, employees may also wear a red sweater or coat.”

The Texan convenience chain has developed a cult-following in the US over the years.



Fans have said that they have transformed “necessity into an adventure.”

The world’s largest in Sevierville, Tennessee, offers a wide selection of bagged jerky with an eye-watering amount of flavours and even a brisket station.

Another part comes from the cleanliness of their bathrooms, even winning awards for being spotless.



The first store opened in Clute, Texas, in 1982.

Over 45 stores remain in Texas but the chain has expanded outside the Lone Star State and into places like Alabama, Florida, and South Carolina.

On Buc-ee’s website it says: “Ever since our inception in 1982, we have been committed to providing clean, friendly, and in stock experience for our customers.”

“Regardless of where you may find us, if the store is big ore small, near or far, the mission remains the same.”

News.title: Moment reckless driver mounts pavement to deliberately ram four men after being booted out of casino
News.content:
THIS is the moment a driver deliberately mounted the pavement to mow down four men after being booted out of a casino.

Nadeem Khan, 49, was captured hurtling towards the group in his Nissan Juke as they stood outside Napoleon’s Casino in Bradford, West Yorkshire.



The driver then miraculously missed the men and instead smashed through a line of bollards.

A judge later told Khan: “You could have killed those men.”



The thug has now been jailed for 47 months and banned from the roads for four years and 11 months.

He must also pass an extended re-test before he can legally drive again.



Bradford Crown Court heard Khan had been ushered out of the casino after becoming involved in an altercation.

He drove away but instead of heading home, Khan returned to the scene and deliberately sped towards the men.

Khan was later arrested at home after police found the damaged car abandoned.

The yob was initially charged with four counts of attempted murder but he admitted four alternative offences of attempting to cause grievous bodily harm with intent, as well as dangerous driving.



Judge Sophie McKone told him: “Whatever happened before your offending is absolutely no excuse for what you did.”

She added: “You mounted the pavement. You crashed through bollards and it was clearly your intention to cause those four men really serious harm.

“At the time none of the men posed any sort of risk to you.

“Whatever had happened has finished.

“You could have got in your car and driven away, but you made a decision to do that.”

News.title: Middlesbrough fire live: Two house fire 'murders' may be linked to organised crime
News.content:
Families 'facing unimaginable loss'

Cllr Adam Brook, Deputy Mayor of Redcar and Cleveland and a Grangetown Ward Councillor, said: "I am absolutely devastated to learn that two people have tragically lost their lives following this morning’s house fire in Grangetown.

“My deepest condolences go to their families, loved ones and friends. Behind today’s headlines are two people who were part of our community, and families who are now facing an unimaginable loss.

“My thoughts are also with those who remain in hospital following the fire, and with their families and loved ones at what will be an incredibly worrying and difficult time. I sincerely hope they make a full recovery.

“Grangetown is a close-knit community and people are understandably shocked and deeply saddened by what has happened. Many residents have been in touch throughout the morning, and I know the whole community will want to support those affected.

“I would like to pay tribute to our emergency services and everyone involved in responding to this devastating incident, who have been working in incredibly difficult circumstances.

“As investigations continue, I would urge people not to speculate or share unconfirmed information about what has happened. There are grieving families at the heart of this tragedy, and they deserve our compassion, dignity, space and privacy.

“This is an incredibly sad day for Grangetown. We are a strong community, and I know we will come together and support one another in the difficult days and weeks ahead.

“My thoughts remain first and foremost with the two people we have tragically lost, their families and loved ones, and everyone affected by today’s devastating events.”

News.title: British woman missing in Benidorm as family haven't heard from her in days
News.content:
British woman missing in Benidorm as family haven't heard from her in days

Alice Rose Chalmers' sister posted on Facebook saying she had not been heard from since Monday after vanishing from the Med Playa Hotel Regente

View 2 Images This images of Alice Rose Chalmers has been shared on Facebook (Image: Facebook)

A British woman has gone missing from a hotel in Benidorm, with her family asking for help in tracking her down.

‌



Alice Rose Chalmers hasn't been heard from since just after midday on Monday, her sister said in a post on Facebook.

‌



The Brit was staying at a hotel in the holiday hotspot when she went missing, according to the social media post.

‌



Her sister Charlotte has issued a desperate plea as the family seek help.

“Alice was initially staying at the Med Playa Hotel Regente, but hotel staff have informed myself that Alice has not been seen back at this hotel since around Monday 24th August lunchtime,” her sister wrote. “Alice is likely staying at a different hotel but this is unknown.”

View 2 Images Med Playa Hotel Regente, Benidorm

‌



“She has not been in contact with any of her family or friends since Monday 24th August around 12:05pm. “She has stopped replying to messages and her phone now goes to voicemail.

The latest possible sighting of Alice was yesterday at around 5:30pm in a pharmacy called Cristin Batres in Avenida Mediterannia area of Benidorm, her sister said.

However, she added: “The information provided does sound like this could be Alice but it is not a confirmed sighting by police yet. She has still not been located.”

Article continues below

The social media post also called for an end to speculation around the mental health of Alice, her sister said: "I know people are trying to help find my sister, which me, my family and Alice's friends really appreciate and are very grateful for, but please stop with all the incorrect speculation on this case without knowing the full background."

Her sister said Alice had been officially reported to the police as a missing person and the family was liaising with Spanish police.

News.title: Dolly Parton's heartbreaking final days as country legend battled cancer
News.content:
Penguin Books reveal letters Dolly sent to encourage young readers

In an Instagram post, Penguin Books revealed that Dolly wrote letters to children who benefitted from the Imagination Library, encouraging them to keep reading.

The letter read: "Dear Imagination Library Graduate,

"My how time flies. It seems it was only yesterday when your family and friends read you your first story. You were just a baby. Now you're five years old and about to go to school. How exciting!

"This may be your last book from my Imagination library but you have to promise me you will keep on reading. If you go to your locla public library you will find a great number of books just for kids your age. Every book is a trasure and every time you open one up, you mill meet new friends and take wonderful journeys to magical places.

"I hope you have a great time in school. I bet your school will even have a library where you can check out books. You and all of your friends are very special. THere is no limit to what you can do or how far you can go. Just remember the lessons my family taught me - dream big dreams, learn everything you can learn, and care for all those who care for you. You do all of these things and you can be anyone you want to be.

"You are terrific, and remember... I will always love you. Dolly."

News.title: Dealer who was last person to see Jay Slater alive 'marries drug mule mum' who helped smuggle £14m of cannabis
News.content:
Dealer who was last person to see Jay Slater alive 'marries drug mule mum' who helped smuggle £14m of cannabis

Drug dealer Ayub Qassim, 33, gave Jay Slater a lift in his car before he vanished in Tenerife in 2024 and he has now wed Paige Crisp, who is due to be sentenced on October for drug smuggling

View 4 Images Ayub Qassim was one of the last people to see Jay Slater before he disappeared (Image: western mail)

The last person to see tragic teenager Jay Slater alive has married a drug dealer mum who faces years behind bars for helping to smuggle almost £14million worth of cannabis.

‌



Ayub Qassim tied the knot with 24-year-old Paige Crisp in a traditional Islamic wedding last year, it has emerged. The ceremony is said to have taken place in Thailand, the same country Crisp and her gang smuggled drugs from. She and ten other Brits were convicted last week.

‌



Jay was on his first holiday without his parents, attending a music festival, when he went missing in Tenerife on June 17 2024. It took 29 days for his body to be found. He’d suffered a catastrophic fall on his way back to his accommodation after a night out with pals.

‌



View 4 Images The AirBnB where Jay spent some of his final hours (Image: Andy Commins / Daily Mirror)

Jay Slater and the forgotten missing of Tenerife - other Brits who have vanished on island READ MORE :

Qassim invited 19-year-old Jay back to his AirB&B on the island after a rave, sparking a month-long hunt for the apprentice bricklayer. He and friend Steven Roccas had given Jay a lift back to their cottage but the teen set off for a bus the next morning with little battery on his mobile phone. He was discovered weeks later dead in a ravine.

33-year-old Qassim, who served a nine year prison sentence for drug offences, married the single mum in 2025, despite a trial hanging over her. In a series of loved-up photos posted on social media, she can be seen snuggling up to Qassim, who himself was jailed after masterminding a sophisticated operation to flood Wales with Class A drugs. The one-time ringleader of a London gang imported heroin and crack cocaine to Cardiff.

‌



View 4 Images Jay Slater died after trying to walk home through rocky terrain

In one clip, he posts: "I never knew how powerful love was until it came to me, in the form of you". In another, she appears to be dressed for a wedding, with henna tattoos on the back of her hands.

Crisp, 24, was one of 11 British nationals stopped by Border Force after a total of 460kg of cannabis was discovered in 22 suitcases. The group had travelled from Thailand via Charles de Gaulle Airport in Paris before being arrested at Birmingham Airport on August 9, 2024.

‌



Each member of the gang was carrying two large suitcases containing around 20kg of cannabis. The bags were so heavy that the group paid an excess baggage charge at Bangkok Airport so they could be placed in the aircraft's hold. The cannabis had a street value of £13.8m.

View 4 Images Paige Crisp was convicted of being involved in helping smuggle over £13m of cannabis in suitcases (Image: Jam Press/National Crime Agency)

Crisp, from Malvern, Worcestershire, was convicted on August 19 of attempting to carry, remove, deposit, harbour, keep, conceal and deal with Class B drugs with intent to evade prohibition on importing. She was among the final three members of the group to be convicted at Birmingham Crown Court.

Article continues below

She appeared alongside Tasia Nelson, 22, of Newquay, Cornwall, and Jaden Ramen, 23, of Merton, London. Crisp, Nelson and Ramen are due to be sentenced on October 22.

Adam Chatfield, Head of Border Force Midlands Command, said: "These convictions should be a stark warning to anyone considering bringing cannabis into the UK. The young people involved now face a serious crime on their records, damaging their job prospects and life chances.

"More than ever, we are working closely with law enforcement partners in the UK and overseas to combat drug smuggling, keep our communities safe and our borders secure."

News.title: Terrified mum claims to have photographed a PANTHER prowling through her Northampton estate
News.content:
Terrified mum claims to have photographed a PANTHER prowling through her Northampton estate

The mum-of-eight says she fears for children living nearby after photographing the mysterious creature, weeks after another suspected big cat was spotted in Northamptonshire

View 3 Images The photo shared by Clare Hodges which she claims she took near her home (Image: Clare Hodges / SWNS)

A terrified mum says she ran for her life after coming face-to-face with a huge black animal she believes was a panther prowling near her home.

‌



Clare Hodges, 51, had stepped outside to put her bins out when a noise behind her caught her attention in the Ryehill area of Northampton. Expecting to see a fox known to visit the neighbourhood, the mum-of-eight instead spotted a large black creature with a long tail just yards from nearby homes.

‌



Clare managed to take a photograph before racing back inside, where she showed the startling image to her partner Joseph. The full-time carer, who looks after her autistic 11-year-old daughter, said: “It was terrifying. I was putting the bins out when I heard a noise behind me.

‌



View 3 Images Clare believes the animal may have made its way from Harlestone Firs Forest (Image: Tony Kershaw / SWNS)

Wild beavers could return to UK area in bid to reduce flood risk and protect against drought READ MORE :

Fox found hiding in cupboard in MP's Westminster office before being escorted out READ MORE :

“ The neighbours had been leaving out some raw lamb for a lovely vixen we have in the area at the minute and we’d been trying to get a photo of it for some time so I had my camera ready already. So I thought it was the fox and turned to get a quick image and then within a second or so I thought ‘oh s**t, what is that?’.

"It was very big and I just ran quicker than I have ever done in my life into the house, shut the door and showed my partner Joseph. I thought it could be a big dog at first, like a Dalmatian with no spots, but then we saw the tail was not like a dog at all.”

‌



Clare says she is now frightened about what could be roaming so close to families’ homes. She told Sell Your Story: “It’s actually terrifying how close to homes it has decided to get. Panthers can be extremely quick and could have got either one of us if it had wanted. I’m worried for the safety of my daughter and other children in the area now.

“She lives in her own little bubble due to her autism so it’s really aware of danger. The other weird thing is that all the cats in the area hadn’t been out for a few days before it happened. So I wonder if its been the area for some time. I think it must have been attracted to the meat which had been laid out in the street for the fox.”

View 3 Images People are questioning whether Clare used artificial intelligence (Image: Tony Kershaw / SWNS)

‌



Clare believes the animal may have made its way from Harlestone Firs Forest, a large area of woodland a couple of miles from her home where she says there have previously been rumours of big cat sightings. She added: “There have been rumours of big cat sightings up there before but what is worrying is how far it came into a built up area. Its a quiet area here but there’s still lots of houses and flats so it’s extremely worrying.”

But not everyone was convinced by Clare’s extraordinary picture after she shared it online, with some questioning whether the image had been created using artificial intelligence. Clare insists the photograph is genuine. She said: “Afterwards I posted the image on my Facebook page and while some people were amazed others didn’t believe me.

"Some said it was AI but it really isn’t - I wouldn’t know how to do that anyway and I don’t have the time to looking after my daughter. Put people can think what they like, but we know what we saw. A lot of people have pointed out the panther like features. Some said they had never seen a clearer picture of a big cat before and never before so close to homes.”

Article continues below

Big cat expert Tim Whittard said: “If authentic then this shows a very large feline animal alarmingly close to people’s homes.” The apparent sighting comes just weeks after another large cat was reportedly spotted elsewhere in Northamptonshire.

There have been a number of possible big cat sightings across Northamptonshire and neighbouring Rutland over the years, including tales surrounding the so-called Beast of Rutland. Northamptonshire Police confirmed they received a report on August 6 of a large cat seen in fields in a village near Corby but said Clare’s latest reported sighting had not been reported to the force.

News.title: The AA warned authorities over wrong-way motorway social media trend last year
News.content:
The AA warned authorities over wrong-way motorway social media trend last year

EXCLUSIVE: The motoring body say they sounded the warning over young motorists driving the wrong-way on motorways and posting their reckless actions on social media in 2025

View 5 Images Police have condemned the 'absolutely unacceptable' actions of drivers following a deadly seven days (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Authorities were warned about the terrifying wrong-way motorway social media trend last year, the AA have said.

‌



The British motoring association stressed more must be done to combat the issue with young drivers after 12 people died inside just seven days in similar crashes. Fears are growing about the deadly consequences of reckless motorists performing dangerous stunts in the quest for plaudits and approval on platforms such as TikTok.

‌



The government has urged social media companies to remove all posts celebrating the foolish acts, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham branded the sharing of footage "truly reprehensible".

‌



The outcry comes after two police officers died when a car travelling the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into their vehicle. PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, were killed on the A66 near Middlesbrough on Saturday. Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae and Cole Robert Worthy, both 17, also died at the scene.

View 5 Images PC Matthew Blades' marked vehicle was struck by a car travelling the wrong way (Image: Cleveland Police/PA Wire)

Earlier this month, five teenagers were killed in a head-on crash while they were driving the wrong way down the motorway in County Kildare, Ireland, in the early hours of the morning. Three women and a seven-year-old boy were rushed to hospital where they were treated for serious injuries.

‌



The motoring body's president Edmund King says authorities were aware there of the perilous trend long before the recent crashes.

He told the Mirror: “Last year, the AA warned of the dangers of more people driving the wrong way on motorways and dual carriageways and also highlighted the trend of some people posting on social media.

5 View 5 Images Tom Clough, who also died in the crash (Image: Cleveland Police/PA Wire) 5 View 5 Images The PM vowed to take action to stop the dangerous driving trend (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"In the 12 months to May 2026 there were 947 cases on English motorways. Yet in the last week alone we have seen two devasting cases with 5 dead on the M9 in County Kildare and 7 dead on the A66 Redcar including two police officers.

"This is such a devasting waste of lives and our thoughts are with the police, the families and friends of all involved and the emergency services who must deal with the traumatic results. “There is some evidence particularly in Eire that videos depicting youths speeding against traffic - often with Garda blue lights in the background - appear on social media. There are now calls for social media to act more quickly to remove this unlawful content that seems to encourage danger for clicks.

“Many other cases are reckless, impatient drivers who blame sat navs for missing an exit or U-turn on the hard shoulder to evade congestion. There is no excuse and 31 drivers in the past 30 weeks were charged for such criminal offences.

‌



View 5 Images The line-of-duty deaths left the country shocked and angry (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

“The spate of recent tragic car crashes is deeply worrying and the consequences last for every. We need more concerted efforts to reduce the carnage of more than 4 deaths each day or 1,538 deaths on our roads each year.”

The AA previously backed a proposal to prevent new drivers under the age of 21 from carrying passengers their own age for six months after they pass their tests.

‌



Sparking a debate about stricter rules for young motorists, they said similar systems in other countries have significantly cut road deaths and injuries.

An AA survey in 2024 shows some support for these measures, with 33 per cent of respondents backing passenger restrictions for new drivers.

But the government held back, raising concerns about how such changes could impact job opportunities for teenagers and young people.

Article continues below

The Government have vowed to "take action" to stop the trend of dangerous driving videos being posted online. Speaking to Channel 5 News, the Prime Minister was asked if there is anything the Government can do to crack down on the "growing problem online of the police being goaded and provoked".

Mr Burnham said: "There's always something we can do and the glorification of dangerous driving is an appalling trend, and it needs to be challenged, and that means everybody playing their part to stop it, including the tech companies."

Pressed on whether he would be asking tech companies to take down such content, he added: "I'm waiting for a full investigation into what happened at the weekend, but people can be sure that we'll take action off all of the issues that are coming out."

News.title: Thousands of people claiming benefits including Universal Credit will get paid early this week
News.content:
Thousands of people claiming benefits including Universal Credit will get paid early this week

If you are due to be paid early you will get your normal amount into your regular bank account. But if you do get paid early, it is worth remembering that you will have a longer wait until your next benefit payment

View 2 Images DWP benefits are being paid early this week (Image: Getty)

Millions of people who claim benefits will get paid early this week because of the August bank holiday.

The government is bringing forward benefit payments to Friday, August 28. You will be paid early if your benefit payment was originally due to land in your bank account on Monday, August 31.

The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) and HMRC do not pay benefit payments on bank holidays. But if you do get paid early, it is worth remembering that you will have a longer wait until your next benefit payment. This means you will have to make your money last longer.

View 2 Images DWP does not pay benefits on bank holidays (Image: Getty)

Child Benefit warning for millions of parents as payments could stop after August 31 READ MORE :

If you are due to get paid early, you will get paid your normal amount and your money should go into your regular bank account as normal. The benefits that will be impacted include Universal Credit, Personal Independence Payment and Carer's Allowance - you can find a full list below.

Minister for Social Security and Disability Sir Stephen Timms said: "We’re pleased to confirm that benefit payments due on the August bank holiday will be paid earlier. This will help ensure families and older people receive their money without disruption over the bank holiday period."

News.title: Murder probe as two people dead in house fire in Middlesbrough
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after two people died in a house fire.

The blaze in Grangetown, Middlesbrough, broke out just before 05:30 BST and also left a woman in hospital in a critical condition, alongside a further three people who suffered non-life threatening injuries.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating what had happened but was "keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time".

The fire happened about two miles from the A66 crash that killed five young men and two police officers on Saturday morning.

Redcar and Cleveland Local Policing Commander Supt Emily Harrison said the force was working to "establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened".

"We will have a high visibility presence in the Grangetown area as this investigation progresses, and to provide reassurance to local communities, who will no doubt be impacted by this tragic incident."

Patrols have been increased in the local area to "reassure the local community", the force said.

News.title: Prince Harry and Meghan land in UK days after announcing move
News.content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in the UK, BBC News understands.

Prince Harry, Meghan and their children Archie and Lilibet are believed to have flown into the country privately from California, and landed in Birmingham shortly before midday.

A spokesman for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex said "this is not something we would comment on".

There did not appear to be a police presence as Harry and his family left the airport, a source told the BBC.

Last week, it was reported that the couple would be relocating to the UK in August. They will not return to official duties but will live in Britain as non-working royals.

It is thought the family will base themselves at a private property outside of London in the Cotswolds area.

Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in school and the new term is due to start next week.

The Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.

King Charles was told of the move earlier this month. The family visited the King at his Highgrove home in July this year, but it is understood the move was not discussed.

Before that visit, Prince Harry and Meghan had not been in the UK together since they attended the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022.

News.title: Heart, hope and a steely determination: Dolly Parton's musical legacy
News.content:
In 1980, Dolly Parton was filming her first Hollywood movie, 9 To 5, and between scenes she had an idea for the tune that would become the movie's theme song.

But her guitar was banned from the set - so she made the beat by strumming her acrylic nails together.

The sound, she realised, was just like the typewriter used by her character, a married secretary who is constantly belittled and sexually harassed by her boss.

Excited, she ran over and sang the song to her co-stars Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda, who was also the film's producer.

"Lily and I looked at each other and we had goosebumps," Fonda said. "And we knew, this is not just a movie song, this is an anthem."

News.title: From 'dirt poor' to philanthropic superstar - the life of Dolly Parton
News.content:
Iconic country musician Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, her family announced on her social media.

"Sadness lies with us, not with Dolly," Parton's nephew Brian Seaver said in a video announcement.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote in excess of 3,000 songs.

Parton took her writing seriously, and considered herself a songwriter over everything else. "It's my way of expressing myself," she said. "It's my therapy."

She was also a savvy businesswoman who wasn't afraid to make tough decisions. Armed with a quick wit and southern charm, she took control of her show business career that spanned more than 60 years.

Follow for live updates and read more about Dolly's life.

News.title: Ex-chief constable investigated over ban on Israeli Maccabi Tel Aviv fans
News.content:
Maccabi supporters were barred from travelling to the game following safety concerns based on an inaccurate report prepared by West Midlands Police.

Eight errors were found in the report, including overstating Maccabi supporters' role in disorder in Amsterdam in 2024, and a reference to a non-existent game between Maccabi and West Ham, said to have been produced by Microsoft Copilot.

His Majesty's Chief Inspector of Constabulary, Sir Andy Cooke, said that confirmation bias had influenced the way West Midlands Police reached and communicated its recommendation over the banning of Maccabi Tel Aviv fans.

"I have several other concerns including, but not limited to, inaccurate information in written communication, a failure to engage with the local Jewish community early enough and poor record keeping and retention of important information," he said.

The decision to impose the ban was made by Birmingham's Safety Advisory Group (SAG), external, which included representatives from bodies including West Midlands Police and Birmingham City Council.

The IOPC said evidence indicated that Guildford "may have had oversight on an intelligence briefing document presented to the safety advisory group (SAG) that was later reported to have contained inaccuracies and misleading information".

It is alleged the briefing document "gave an imbalanced view of the risk away fans posed", contributing to the decision to ban the supporters.

The police watchdog added: "We consider Mr Guildford may have failed to ensure due diligence and the highest level of scrutiny over such an influential document."

Guildford retired from the force after both Downing Street and the home secretary said they had lost confidence in his leadership.

Announcing his retirement, Guildford did not offer an apology and blamed what he described as the "political and media frenzy" for his decision to step down.

It is understood that if gross misconduct is proven against Guildford at a misconduct hearing, he would likely be placed on the barred list which would prevent him from working in policing in the future.

News.title: Rockstar Games breaks silence on Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks
News.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Clips appearing to show gameplay and cinematics from the title began appearing online last week, but the developer did not acknowledge them straight away.

In a statement, the company said the leaks had been "heartbreaking" for the team working on the sequel, and that they were "not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time".

The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.

When leaks first began to surface, there was some doubt as to whether they were genuine.

But as the days went on, evidence mounted to suggest they were legitimate.

Copies of clips were quickly taken down from social media sites via copyright strikes, where the owner of a work can request its removal.

And, on Friday, Rockstar's parent company Take Two Interactive launched legal proceedings regarding the leaks in a New York court.

Rockstar acknowledged players had been waiting for it to address the leaked footage, and said it was "unfortunate the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers".

It also thanked fans who sent messages of support over the past week, adding: "Your words have meant more to the team than you can imagine."

The group behind the leaks claims to be acting in the interests of players, accusing Rockstar of engaging in anti-consumer practices such as its decision not to release a disc version of GTA 6 at launch.

Not everyone is convinced, as each release of new material has invited viewers to send cryptocurrency "donations" to the user uploading them.

News.title: CIA chief met Russian intelligence services but not Putin, Kremlin says
News.content:
The head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) met figures from Russia's intelligence services during his unannounced visit to Moscow on Tuesday, the Kremlin has confirmed.

John Ratcliffe travelled to the Russian capital on Tuesday but neither side has shed any light on what prompted the unconventional meeting or what was discussed.

It is rare for American senior intelligence leaders to travel to Russia, with the last comparable meeting taking place in the months leading up to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Ratcliffe arrived in Moscow on board a military plane which left later the same day.

The Kremlin ruled out speculation the CIA head met Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"There were contacts with the intelligence services," Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

"There were no meetings with the president of Russia. That's all I can say on the subject. Naturally, President Putin is briefed immediately about everything," he added.

Peskov made the comments in response to a question at his daily press briefing from a reporter at the Russian newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta, who asked if Vladimir Putin was informed about the CIA chief meetings and "at what level" they were held.

Putin's spokesman was also asked by the BBC's Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg what was the topic of the CIA talks.

"I have nothing to add to what I've already said on the subject," Peskov replied.

It was too early to say what impact this meeting would have over repairing bilateral US-Russian relations, he said, telling reporters: "How much this will impact the overall process of recovering our bilateral relations from the profound crisis they're currently in, it is premature to say."

But contacts between intelligence agencies are "a positive phenomenon, a positive process," Peskov added, saying they often continue "even during the most difficult moments" in relations between the two countries.

Ahead of the trip, the US told Ukraine that a senior delegation would be travelling to Moscow and asked Kyiv to suspend strikes until they had left, a senior Ukrainian official told CBS.

There has been no official comment on Ratcliffe's visitfrom the CIA, White House or Pentagon.

Ratcliffe appears to be one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit Russia during President Donald Trump's second term.

The last time a CIA director visited Moscow was in November 2021, when William Burns warned Russia against sending troops into Ukraine. Weeks later, the Kremlin launched its full-scale war on Ukraine.

Since then, the US has had strained relations with Russia, which has been isolated on the world stage and faced international economic sanctions.

Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year but the meeting did not lead to a breakthrough. Subsequent US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled.

John Foreman, who served as a British military attachÃ© to Moscow between 2019 and 2022, told Radio 4's PM programme: "The Americans don't normally send such a high ranking official to Moscow unannounced at short notice unless something is up."

News.title: Dad of woman who took her own life says Treasury failed in its duty of care
News.content:
The father of a civil service employee who took her own life the day after a meeting with her managers has said the lack of support given to her by the Treasury "beggars belief".

Chloe Moffat, 26, a personal assistant to a Treasury director, died on 20 May last year, after she was told of allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information about colleagues, which she denied.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, David Moffat said he did not feel the Treasury had taken responsibility for its part in her death.

He added that her loss was "devastating", and had "torn such a big hole in our lives".

The Treasury said "it will learn the lessons from this tragedy".

On 19 May 2025, Chloe went to what she thought was a routine one-to-one with her line manager, but a more senior manager was also present.

"Chloe's first comment was, 'Oh, this must be serious, there's two of you here'", David told Today's Emma Barnett. "So that's the first time that she was aware of anything [that] might be a to do."

"And then they worked through and put several allegations to her that she'd shared confidential information."

During the meeting, David said she had asked on several occasions if she would lose her job, and if she could have a friend there - both of which were refused.

A coroner found at an inquest earlier in August that the Treasury did not apply written disciplinary policy, which would have made clear that if the allegations against Chloe were proven, the likely penalty was a written warning, not dismissal.

"Even though she asked, they said they could not determine the outcome," David said.

Straight after the meeting, Chloe was locked out of her emails. "That was all part of the shock and awe of it all for Chloe," David said.

The coroner found that the meeting between Chloe and her managers "materially contributed" to her death.

News.title: Yellow warnings remain in force as rain and thunderstorms hit parts of UK
News.content:
Downpours and thunderstorms will continue to bring the risk of flooding to parts of the UK on Wednesday.

A Met Office yellow warning for thunderstorms is valid until 22:00 BST, and was amended on Wednesday morning to cover northern and eastern Wales, as well as north-west England, the Midlands and parts of eastern and southern England.

The rain could be heavy enough to bring flash flooding and travel disruption, with lightning and large hail posing additional hazards.

Another Met Office yellow warning is in place for Thursday, when more thunderstorms are expected.

For some areas that have seen barely any rain so far this August, the next few days could bring the wettest weather in many weeks.

News.title: Nicotine vapes best chance to quit smoking, major review finds
News.content:
Smokers who want to quit have the best chance of doing so if they use nicotine e-cigarettes, a review has found.

The Cochrane team looked at 80 major trials involving nearly 30,000 people and found that nicotine vapes were more effective than traditional aids such as patches, gum and support plans - increasing the success rate by about 60%, from around six in every 100 managing to quit smoking to one in every 10.

They outperformed non-nicotine vapes too, although researchers say switching to these afterwards might help with weaning off nicotine.

And they could prove more effective than the new anti-smoking pill cytisine, external, which the NHS has started to roll out - although more research is needed.

News.title: 'Ironing board' seats to be replaced on Thameslink
News.content:
"Ironing board" seats on some commuter trains will get extra cushioning, the transport secretary has said, more than a decade after the government spent Â£1.6bn of public money building the fleet.

Heidi Alexander announced that more than 60,000 seats on all 115 Thameslink trains would get new cushions and backrests, replacing much-criticised thin and hard seats.

She said the work, set to begin in 2027 and last two years, was "public ownership of our railways in action" as part of the new Great British Railways programme.

However, some have criticised how the Department for Transport (DfT) awarded a Â£1.6bn contract for the trains despite being warned of the seat discomfort at the time.

The seat upgrades are part of wider improvements planned for the Thameslink network after Greater Thameslink Railway came into public ownership in May 2026.

Other measures included an increase in Gatwick Express services from December and a programme to refurbish train toilets and remove graffiti across the fleet.

Alexander said: "We'll start getting rid of the dreaded 'ironing board seats' so passengers can enjoy comfier, more pleasant journeys on some of Britain's busiest commuter routes."

She said wider rail reforms would continue under the planned Great British Railways organisation, which is intended to oversee rail services across England.

The class-700 Thameslink trains were heralded by the DfT as "state-of-the-art" and "a fantastic deal" for taxpayers when they were rolled out between 2016 and 2019.

That followed the DfT spending Â£1.6bn of taxpayers' money for German manufacturer Siemens to build the trains in 2013, following a bidding process which began in 2008.

DfT's own procurement guidance document for the fleet, seen by the BBC, stressed that they should be "high capacity" and "reduced weight".

It said the new electric fleet would have a design that "must cater for [about] 1,000 people to board or alight at one time" and a "2+2 seat layout to ease flow and provide standing space".

Some have claimed that this aim to maximise capacity and standing space for commuters led to the seats being so thinly cushioned.

Responding to Alexander's post on X praising the new re-cushioning project, Graeme Pickering, senior correspondent at Railway Magazine, wrote: "Might have been wise not to frame this as 'public ownership fixes private sector mess' when it was the DfT which procured said trains."

Two years before the Thameslink trains were rolled out to the public, a prototype was unveiled at London's Excel centre in 2014.

News.title: Reform proposes £30 tax rebate for HMRC phone delays
News.content:
People on hold to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) for more than 30 minutes would get Â£30 off their tax bill under a Reform UK government, Robert Jenrick has announced.

Reform's economy spokesman said HMRC's treatment of taxpayers was "offensive to working people" and his party would tie the pay of senior HMRC officials to customer service targets.

To prevent abuse, the tax credit for phone delays would be limited to two occasions in a given tax year, Jenrick said.

HMRC has said it has improved its response times since a highly critical report by a committee of MPs, external, in January 2025, accused the organisation of seeking to "degrade its telephone service to drive taxpayers to digital channels".

The Public Accounts Committee report said nearly 44,000 customers were cut off without warning after being on hold for more than an hour in 2024 and "HMRC's treatment of taxpayers has damaged trust in the tax system".

Jenrick highlighted the findings - which were rejected as "completely baseless" by the then boss of HMRC - at a media conference in central London.

"Frankly, it is offensive to working people and I have had enough," said the former Tory MP.

"So, we will give HMRC a big incentive to actually provide proper customer service.

"I'm announcing today that under a Reform government, if you spend more than half an hour waiting for HMRC to answer your call, you will get a Â£30 credit off your tax bill. If HMRC delay, they can repay.

"And to make sure that the staff actually hit their targets, we'll tie the pay of senior HMRC officials to their customer service performance."

Jenrick also pledged to scrap UK privacy rules in favour of a "light-touch" approach to data protection as part of a bid to slash "red tape" for businesses.

He said the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which mirrors EU legislation and was adopted as domestic law after Brexit, had "strangled" tech firms and small enterprises.

The framework would be replaced by rules modelled on New Zealand's privacy legislation, which Reform says has the lightest-touch regime still recognised as being "adequate" by the EU.

Labour accused Reform of wanting to "scrap vital safeguards that protect people's private data" with its "unworkable and unserious plans".

HMRC has been contacted for a response.

News.title: Household energy bills to hit three-year high as Ofgem announces 4% rise from October
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham acknowledged people would find the increase "difficult" but highlighted his move to cut VAT from electricity bills, which he said would help from October.

He said the government would "continue to look... at how we get energy prices down in the long term".

As well as the VAT cut, the government said the warm homes discount would take Â£150 off bills for six million households this winter.

But analysts at the energy consultancy Cornwall Insight have forecast domestic energy prices may rise a further 9% in the new year, bringing renewed concern to households during the coldest months.

Shadow energy secretary Claire Coutinho said the government must "put cheap energy first", saying while it had promised to cut bills by Â£300 they had "gone up by nearly Â£400 instead".

Liberal Democrat spokesperson for energy and net zero Pippa Heylings said Burnham needed to "wake up to the scale of the challenge" and make bold changes to lower bills.

Reform UK treasury spokesperson Robert Jenrick said households faced a "difficult period ahead" and said Labour's "net zero ideology" is driving up bills.

Former Prime Minister Gordon Brown also weighed in, saying the government should introduce a "machine gaming tax" and use proceeds to help those struggling with bills.

Longer term, he said Burnham should look at a social tariff for energy.

"I think Andy Burnham, I know him well, will want to do something along the lines I'm suggesting," he said.

Neil Kenward, Ofgem's director general for markets, said while gas bills were rising by 8%, electricity bills were actually falling slightly due to the government's VAT cut.

He said the gap between gas and electricity bills meant it would be cheaper for households to transition to heat pumps.

News.title: Young care leavers dying early a 'national tragedy'
News.content:
Young adults who have left care have a death rate around four times higher than the general population, a new review, external shows.

Often left alone "with no safety net," the report says the consequences can be catastrophic.

On turning 18, people leaving care in England often lose "significant levers of support", the Government-commissioned report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4 Today, report co-author and broadcaster Ashley John-Baptiste, who grew up in care, called the deaths a national tragedy.

There were 112 deaths of care leavers aged 18 to 24 notified in 2025, which the review said equalled about 130 deaths per 100,000 care leavers.

John-Baptiste recalled his own experience of turning 18 and moving out of the last of four foster homes he'd lived in.

"I was made to live alone and work out how to be an adult," he said.

Unable to afford a bed frame, he says he slept on a mattress on the floor of his council flat and felt a deep sense of abandonment and isolation.

News.title: NHS failing child sexual abuse victims in adulthood, say psychiatrists
News.content:
People sexually abused as children who seek help in later life for mental health problems are being failed by the NHS, senior doctors have told the BBC.

The Royal College of Psychiatrists is issuing a public apology for what it says is decades of mismanagement and misdiagnosis in the UK.

For some, it has worsened their traumas, it said.

The college said mental health staff have been too focussed on treating symptoms rather than exploring how past traumatic experiences can still affect patients.

Support is improving, it said, but there must be better training and more investment - something NHS bosses have said is being introduced.

The apology has been included in a report, external by the college and given to the BBC.

Immediate past president of the college, Dr Lade Smith, said she was "sorry" that, too often, victims have suffered "avoidable harm when seeking help".

The report details how treatment has sometimes been inappropriate, while people have been re-traumatised by the experience of repeated assessments and history-taking and not always being believed.

Dr Smith told the BBC it was clear people were not getting the support they needed, and that this was not just a failing of psychiatrists, but the whole mental health system.

"Services are so fragmented. The system is set up to provide short, discrete episodes of care. Psychiatrists do not get the time to build up a relationship with patients so they can be properly supported.

"They are lucky if they get eight sessions of therapy, when it could take eight sessions for a person just to disclose the abuse.

"And these are just the people who get support â many don't even get seen by mental health services because services are so stretched," she said.

A student who escaped conflict in Sudan to live in the UK described passing his GCSE exams in maths and English as "one of the proudest moments in my life".

Nasser Hamid, from Ipswich, secured grade four passes in both subjects, picking up his maths grade on Thursday after passing English earlier this year.

The 20-year-old aspires to be a football referee after an injury halted his goal of becoming a professional player.

At Suffolk New College, he is taking an IT course aimed at an engineering career alongside his refereeing plans.

On finding out he now has his English and maths qualifications, Nasser said: “I feel proud – it is one of the proudest moments in my life – this is the result I was waiting for to step forward.

“Thanks to Suffolk New College, without their help I wouldn’t be standing here.”

open image in gallery Nasser Hamid, of Ipswich, achieved grade four passes in both subjects, collecting his maths result on Thursday, having passed English earlier this year ( Suffolk New College )

Nasser recently oversaw a charity football match at Ipswich Town’s ground, Portman Road, and said he would love to referee at a future World Cup.

He also officiates at Saturday and Sunday league games.

“I started at grass roots level and recently had the pleasure of stepping out at Portman Road – one of the greatest stadiums in England,” he said.

“It was eye-opening.

“I recently went to the Edinburgh International Cup.

“And I’d like to continue to progress, to the Championship, the Premier League and with the World Cup – who knows.”

open image in gallery Nasser Hamid studies at Suffolk New College, where he is also taking an IT course with a view to an engineering career outside his refereeing ( Suffolk Refugee Support )

Nasser started out as an ESOL (English for Speakers of Other Languages) student at Suffolk New College.

He urged others in a similar position to “just believe in yourself”.

“With discipline and hard work, you can achieve your goals,” he said.

Nasser said he was “pushing forward to be an engineer”.

“I’m on track,” he said.

“Next, I’m going to do an access course and then (hopefully) go to university to study engineering.”

David Squire, head of maths at Suffolk New College, said: “I’ve never been prouder of a learner in my life.”

Top grades for GCSE entries have seen an increase compared with 2025, though overall pass rates have now settled back to pre-pandemic levels, according to national data.

Meanwhile, the results gap between boys and girls has closed further, reaching its smallest margin this century.

Passenger traffic at Dubai International Airport plummeted during the second quarter, officials said Wednesday, after the regional conflict involving Iran disrupted air travel and forced travelers to choose flight paths avoiding the Middle East.

The aviation hub handled 13 million passengers in the second quarter, bringing its total for the first half to 31.5 million. That represents a 31.3% decline compared with the first half of 2025, according to the airport.

Flight operations across the United Arab Emirates and the wider Gulf faced closures and restrictions after the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb. 28. Dubai airport sustained minor damage during Iranian strikes.

Total aircraft movements reached 150,600 over the first half—a 32.1% annual drop—with 62,500 movements recorded in the second quarter.

Planes parked at Dubai International Airport on March 11, 2026 after drones fell near the airport, injuring four people ( AFP via Getty Images )

CEO Paul Griffiths noted, however, that passenger volume grew steadily each month during the second quarter, adding that this momentum is expected to continue.

"The events of the disruption, which lasted two months, that had an impact on traffic," Griffiths told The Associated Press. "However, the trajectory now is universally positive."

He said the airport is awaiting foreign carriers, particularly from Europe, to restart their flights.

"I'm very confident we'll be back to full operation in a very short space of time," he said.

Iran war rages

The conflict between the U.S. and Iran is still raging and the crucial Strait of Hormuz remained closed despite Tehran agreeing on a temporary transit route through the key waterway with Oman.

“The understanding between Iran and Oman does not mean the opening of the Strait of Hormuz,” deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said.

The statement came as Trump threatened to launch new strikes on a nuclear site, as well as Iranian military ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu hailed President Donald Trump's new campaign of economic pressure on Iran but said that a diplomatic deal with Iran does not seem possible, according to AFP.

On Tuesday evening, the leader said: “I doubt, however, that an agreement can be reached with that group there, with those savages. I tell you — an agreement cannot be reached.”

News.content:
