Wissa features in 2.3% of teams at the time of writing.



The deadline for Gameweek 2 is 6:30pm this Friday.

Sports.title: Ipswich set for Liam Delap transfer windfall with Chelsea flop joining Nottingham Forest for eye-watering £50million
Sports.content:
IPSWICH are set to bank £4million when Liam Delap moves from Chelsea to Nottingham Forest.

Striker Delap, 23, is expected to undergo a medical and sign a long-term contract in a £50million move to the City Ground this week.



Delap joined Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m a year ago, and it is understood the Suffolk club inserted a clause to receive 20 per cent of any future profits.

This would give newly-promoted Ipswich, who have been one of the big spenders this summer, a £4m boost.



Ipswich have splashed more than £150m in transfers so far this summer, a figure beaten only by Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, Newcastle and Tottenham.

Among those signings were Julio Enciso, Emersonn, Abdul Fatawu and Abdoul Ouattara in a collection of 12 new permanent signings.



They have already surpassed the figure they spent when they were last promoted into the top flight, and have already gotten off to a better start than then as well.

Ipswich took 11 games to win a game in the Premier League in 2024/25 before they beat Spurs on November 10.

However, last Saturday they got off to a winning start with a 2-1 win over Sunderland thanks to goals from Emersonn and Jack Clarke.

Delap netted 12 goals for Ipswich before his move to Chelsea.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But he flopped for the Blues, picking up more yellow cards for the Blues (seven) than goals scored (three).

Nicolas Jackson looks set to join Delap in leaving Chelsea, with Aston Villa edging closer to sealing a £65m deal after personal terms were agreed.

Atletico Madrid are also in talks to land Jackson, but Villa’s expected sale of Ollie Watkins to Al-Hilal will give them the upper hand while the Spanish club attempt to resolve the future of Julian Alvarez.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘could offer Viktor Gyokeres, Gabriel Jesus AND cash for stunning Julian Alvarez transfer worth £128million’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL could offer Viktor Gyokeres AND Gabriel Jesus in part-exchange for Julian Alvarez, according to reports.

The Gunners are keen to recruit the Atletico Madrid superstar ahead of next Tuesday’s transfer deadline.



Former Manchester City star Alvarez has had his heart set on a move to Barcelona.

But Atletico’s reluctance to flog their star man to a LaLiga rival has kept Arsenal in the race.



TRANSFER NEWS LIVE: ALL THE LATEST FROM THE SUMMER WINDOW

Diego Simeone‘s side want Alvarez’s future determined by Friday.

And according to the Independent, Arsenal believe that being able to offer Gyokeres and Jesus could hand them an edge.

Simeone, 56, is determined to bolster his forward line, irrespective of whether Alvarez stays.

Atletico chiefs want £128million for their Argentine forward, a sum they do not believe Barca can pay.

Even if Barcelona do stump up the cash, however, Atleti would have very little time to sign a replacement.

In this instance they could turn to Chelsea misfit Nicolas Jackson, although Aston Villa are currently leading the race.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Arsenal, meanwhile, would need to convince Alvarez to join, even if a part exchange offer featuring Gyokeres and/or Jesus is successful.

The two-time Premier League champion has “softened” his stance towards potentially moving to the Emirates, but would still much prefer Barcelona.

Alvarez has four years remaining on his Atletico contract but has been demanding an exit.

Atletico’s No19 missed his side’s LaLiga opener against Malaga and was jeered by fans as he came off the bench in the 2-2 draw against Villarreal last weekend.

ARSENAL TRANSFER NEWS LIVE: All the latest rumours from the Emirates



Alvarez was said to be “devastated” by the reception he received from supporters, in addition to so far being denied his dream move.

He did not attend training today after complaining of a stomach issue overnight.

Arsenal transfer chief Andrea Berta previously held a similar role at Atletico Madrid and helped negotiate Alvarez’s move from City in 2024.

Berta has not given up hope of signing him again and has reportedly been in contact with his former employers in recent days.

Gabriel Jesus would be a prime candidate to be offered in part exchange, having not made Arsenal’s matchday squad for last Friday’s Prem opener against Coventry or the Community Shield the previous week.



The Brazilian has been linked with a move to Napoli this summer but a deal is yet to materialise.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Gyokeres, meanwhile, did feature as a sub in the Community Shield but was left on the bench against former side Coventry.

An exit after just one year at the Emirates so far cannot be ruled out.

Sports.title: England set to PLAY at next World Cup as Uefa calls off Fifa boycott after getting assurances over sales plan
Sports.content:
UEFA chiefs have dropped their threat to boycott future FIFA tournaments – after less than a month.

Euro bosses made the threat as part of their war with Fifa President Gianni Infantino over his plans to partially sell off the World Cup to private backers.



But Nyon leaders, gathering in Monaco for Thursday’s Champions League draw will confirm that the idea is now OFF the table.

Uefa is pointing to legal guarantees from Fifa that the sell-off plan is dead for god to justify the change of stance.



Representatives of the 55 Uefa member associations will be told that Fifa has given a binding undertaking that the plan – which would have seen Infantino earning £30m per year as chief executive of the combined enterprise – has been abandoned.

In addition, the associations will be told, Uefa has received “assurances that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.



The decision is a relief to the six European women’s under-20 teams, including England, due to play in the looming age group World Cup in Poland.

Uefa is still determined to bring down the curtain on Infantino’s 11-year Fifa reign – although opponents of the current Zurich regime have just two months to find a candidate to stand against the Swiss.

Infantino was among a slew of Fifa executives who received legal demands to preserve all documents and information over the sell-off plan – “Fifa Forward Enterprises” – as part of the Uefa campaign threatening court action.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Canada’s Victor Montagliani, who is close to his country’s Prime Minister Mark Carney and is known to have been angered by Infantino’s decision to ally with US President Donald Trump, is seen as a potential option, along with Bahrain’s Sheikh Salman Al Khalifa.



Earlier this month Uefa insisted it had lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership and that Fifa’s U-turn hadn’t changed its position.

Infantino was forced into a humiliating apology over the failed plans and said “errors were made”.

The joint letter signed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom said: “We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again.



“We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

“With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting.”

Uefa are not the only major organisation to withdraw their support for Infantino.

The English, Welsh and Scottish FAs said it had lost confidence in the Swiss chief ahead of ahead of the Fifa elections in March.

Montagliani is understood to be a major contender to run against Infantino, as well as Uefa president Alexander Ceferin.



The latest move comes the Italian FA, previously a strong backer of Infantino, formally withdrew its support for the Swiss to win a final four-year term as the head of the world game.

FA chief Giovanni Malago said: “We will continue to work alongside Uefa and other European federations to promote a football model based on merit, solidarity, sustainability, and the centrality of fans.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We identify with a model of dialogue, listening, and shared responsibility that has thus far allowed football to grow, innovate, and at the same time defend its founding principles.”

Meanwhile, Brazilian 2002 World Cup winners Cafu and Roberto Carlos have endorsed Infantino’s reign, further indicating the global split over Fifa’s future

Sports.title: Liverpool ‘open talks with Crystal Palace over Ismaila Sarr transfer after ENDING Yankuba Minteh pursuit’
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL have turned their attention towards signing Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr, reports suggest.

Sarr, 28, has been attempting to force his way out of the Selhurst Park club, with Galatasaray the club who were said to be leading the race.



However, Fabrizio Romano has now reported Liverpool are making a move for the Senegal winger.

The report says the Reds have opened talks to sign Sarr after their move for Yankuba Minteh collapsed because of Brighton’s demands over a sale.



An opening bid worth £50million has been sent to kick off the talks.

The move for Sarr could rise to a higher value with Palace reluctant to sell.

Sarr was missing from Palace’s matchday squad to face Everton on the opening day amid transfer interest from Galatasaray.

That game ended in a 2-0 loss, though new boss Pierre Sage insisted his absence was due to recent struggles with a groin injury.

He scored 21 goals last season en route to Palace being crowned Europa Conference League champions.

It’s been claimed Palace want more than £50m to sell the forward, who first joined them from Marseille in 2024.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He had prior experience in England with Watford, having spent four years with the Hornets between 2019 and 2023.

Liverpool have been trying to add more firepower to their team all summer.

They are seemingly unwilling to meet Paris Saint-Germain‘s demands for France World Cup star Bradley Barcola, who is valued at around £145m by the Ligue 1 champions.

Andoni Iraola‘s side were held to a 2-2 draw away at Newcastle, but looked largely toothless in attack with the likes of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz failing to perform.

Sports.title: Solheim Cup captain Nordqvist announces shock mid-season retirement
Sports.content:
Solheim Cup captain Anna Nordqvist has announced via social media that she will retire from playing professional golf after this week's FM Championship, live on Sky Sports.

The three-time major winner will captain Team Europe at Bernardus Golf from September 11-13, having featured in each of the previous nine Solheim Cups as a player and been part of five winning teams.

Nordqvist has been a playing vice-captain in the last two contests but quickly ruled herself out of juggling captaincy with playing against Team USA in the Netherlands, despite still regularly featuring on the LPGA Tour and impressing in the majors.

In a letter posted on social media, Nordqvist added: "Twenty years ago I came to the US with two suitcases, a golf bag and a dream of one day competing with the best golfers in the world.

"I've fallen so many times, but I never gave up and I stood up every time I fell. I am forever thankful for everything this game has given me and the people I have met along the way.

"I am not sure what the future has in store for me, but it is with a grateful heart I have decided to retire from playing professional golf to focus on my health and my family. Thank you to everyone who has supported me in this journey and been part of it along the way. It has meant the world to me."

Sports.title: Man City considering bid for Chelsea's Fernandez
Sports.content:
Manchester City are considering making a bid for Enzo Fernandez before the transfer deadline.

Sky Sports News has reported the midfielder is a top target for City boss Enzo Maresca following Rodri's departure.

City have signed Ayyoub Bouaddi, the highly-rated 18-year-old Morocco international, who impressed at the World Cup.

That deal comes after City spent £116m to sign Elliot Anderson and the club still want to make more additions in midfield, with an interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Roma's Manu Kone.

Chelsea are also considering a late move for Aston Villa goalkeeper Emi Martinez. The Argentina international's representatives have offered Martinez to Chelsea.

Chelsea's current No 1 Robert Sanchez came under criticism after his error in Monday's win at Fulham.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gonzalo Garcia scored after an error from Robert Sanchez

Fernandez to feature vs Luton

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says Fernandez will be involved in their Carabao Cup tie against Luton Town.

Fernandez came off the bench against Fulham on Monday in Chelsea's opening game of the season and the midfielder is set to feature again on Thursday.

"Yes, we expect that he's involved," said Alonso in a press conference on Wednesday.

"He's trained. He's training really well. He's a good professional and he will be involved."

Image: Fernandez played in Chelsea's opening Premier League match at Fulham

Alonso was also asked whether he expected Fernandez to stay at the club.

"We want to have the best team possible," he said.

"We know his qualities; he has shown them, and we have to wait. We'll think about tomorrow and see how things develop."

Analysis: Chelsea-City relationship strained by Maresca and deadline tensions

Image: Fernandez worked with new Man City head coach Enzo Maresca at Chelsea

Sky Sports News' James Savundra:

"Earlier this month, nearly two weeks ago, Chelsea did set a deadline. It was Friday at 5pm, a couple of weeks ago, for clubs to submit a deal and a bid worth up to £120m; that was the asking price for Fernandez. Man City ignored that deadline, but we do know they do retain an interest in signing the player.

"That deadline doesn't actually seem as fixed as it was set by Chelsea a couple of weeks ago, because when I spoke to Xabi Alonso last week, he offered no guarantees when it came to Fernandez.

"He simply said the player was working hard ahead of that game in the Monday Night Football against Fulham. And then what was so interesting in that game was that there were a number of injury issues that Xabi Alonso was having to deal with ahead of his first match in charge, including no Moises Caicedo.

"It would have felt maybe natural that Enzo Fernandez would have come in. But it was Reece James alongside Romeo Lavia in the centre of midfield instead.

"Fernandez did come on the pitch. He got booed by the Fulham supporters. There were plenty of cheers, though, when it came to the Chelsea supporters, because there was a mixed reception when he came off the bench against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge in their final pre-season friendly around 10 days ago.

Image: Fernandez ranked highly in a number of attacking metrics last season

"However, it remains to be seen what sort of negotiation Chelsea would be willing to go into with Manchester City because there clearly is a strained relationship between the two football clubs.

"Chelsea's season was completely derailed by what happened with Enzo Maresca leaving around Christmas time, and Man City had to pay Chelsea £17m in compensation because of their role in that. To wait and see what Chelsea's asking price would be, given that we previously knew it to be around £120m."

"What are Man City willing to pay for a player who seems to be Maresca's top target in this transfer window?

"We know City should have money to spend now because they've sold a record number of players in this transfer window, and we know Maresca loves Fernandez."

Sports.title: Celtic CL post-mortem: What went wrong and where do they go from here?
Sports.content:
Celtic have spent the last couple of years making Champions League qualification look like a problem they simply cannot solve. But even by their recent standards, this was a collapse of remarkable proportions.

Four goals ahead with less than an hour still to play across the tie, Celtic somehow found themselves on the wrong end of a 5-4 aggregate defeat to LASK. A place in the league phase was theirs to lose - and they lost it spectacularly, with individual mistakes, questionable decisions and a team that appeared to run out of answers when the pressure mounted.

The fallout will inevitably focus on Martin O'Neill, who took responsibility for the defeat afterwards. But this feels like a much bigger failure than one manager or one night. It raises questions about the squad Celtic have assembled, the decisions made in the transfer market and whether the club were truly prepared for their biggest test of the season.

So, let's break down Celtic's current situation.

Who is to blame - the board, O'Neill, the players?

O'Neill took full responsibility. But the truth is they are all to blame. Should the Celtic players be blowing a four-goal lead with less than an hour to play? No.

Did individual errors and complacency cost them on the night? Yes.

Did O'Neill make the right subs? Probably not - the team was severely weakened with every change and then, similar to Thomas Tuchel's England against Argentina, they were left with no attacking options when the inevitable happened.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Adam Binnie looks at the effects of Celtic's defeat in the Champions League, what it means for possible transfers and how it will affect the aspirations of Scottish clubs in Europe

But were Celtic fully prepared for this qualifier, compared to last season? They were certainly more prepared.

The signings of Kasper Hogh, Camilo Duran, Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan cost around £32m. They seem to have improved the squad. The starting line-up is stronger. But there were still gaping holes that needed filling.

Celtic knew Arne Engels was likely to leave, but weren't able to replace him in time for LASK. They knew Kieran Tierney needed cover, but they still haven't brought in a back-up left-back. Alistair Johnston's injury was a late blow, but they perhaps should've been ready with a replacement as he was close to leaving before his injury. So, while good signings have been made, they were not fully prepared for this tie.

For a Celtic team to finish a Champions League tie with likes of Dane Murray, Liam Scales, Anthony Ralston and Luke McCowan on the field suggests how threadbare they still are.

Also, it could be argued that postponing their Scottish Premiership match with St Johnstone at the weekend was a mistake, given how dead on their feet the team looked in the second half and in extra time in Austria. Some of them could've done with the extra minutes at the weekend.

What does it mean for transfers?

Missing out on the Champions League could have huge consequences for Celtic in the last week of the transfer window. Celtic would've been guaranteed another £40m from Europe's premier competition. But they know the reality is much more than that, having made around £75m from their Champions League exploits two seasons ago.

Had they made it there last night, they were expecting to spend in excess of £20m this week on a number of players, including Torino's Gvidas Gineitis and Slovan Liberec's Ermin Mahmic. It remains to be seen whether those deals can still be done, but Gineitis certainly seems unlikely given that he would cost around £10m.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic threw away a four goal lead, losing 5-4 to Austrian side Lask which saw Martin O'Neill's side dumped out of the Champions League

When there's Champions League football on offer, there's no doubt you can operate in a different market. The finances that come with it are huge, but also the lure it has on players is a big draw and sometimes a deciding factor on whether they will join a club in the Scottish league. Even up to yesterday afternoon [Tuesday], it's understood Celtic were being offered some top European talent, via intermediaries, who were seeking to play for a Champions League club this season. That's gone now.

Celtic are in the market for a couple of central midfielders, a goalkeeper, left-back, right-back and possibly even a left winger, before next Thursday's deadline. It's a lot of work to do in a week, with a threadbare team of people doing it but the show must go on to fill the gaps in the squad.

While money is likely to be spent on a midfielder and goalkeeper, some of the other positions may now come from loans. The Celtic hierarchy, recruitment team, O'Neill and Maloney are expected to meet this week to discuss the plan of action for the last week of the window.

What's the impact on UEFA coefficients - by Adam Binnie Celtic's Champions League shortcomings have a knock-on effect on fellow Premiership clubs with European ambitions. That's due to Uefa's association club coefficient ranking system, which determines how European places are distributed by assessing the performances of clubs in continental qualification over a five-year period. Although ranking points for wins in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League are the same (two points for a win, one point for a draw) - there are more bonus points up for grabs in UEFA's elite competition. For example, If Celtic were to finish top of the league phase of the Europa League, they would earn 6 bonus points - the same number they would get for finishing rock bottom of the Champions League table. Four years ago, Scotland were ranked ninth in Europe, behind only England, Spain, Germany, France, Italy, Portugal, Netherlands and Belgium. That permitted automatic Champions League entry for league champions as well as an additional spot in qualifying for the runners-up. However, Scotland are now 18th on the list and are almost certain to lose one of its five total European spots this season. League champions will no longer enter Europe's premier competition at the play-off stage and instead must go through three rounds of qualifying before reaching the competition proper.

How do the club avoid another season of protests and constant negativity?

Despite the glorious ending, last season was a bit of a nightmare for everyone involved in Celtic. No Champions League and poor transfer windows led to mass protests against the board, campaigns to boycott merchandise, a managerial resignation, ultras bans, a managerial sacking and a disjointed team that was carried over the line to a double by O'Neill.

There is only one way to avoid a repeat of last season - and that is for the board to go all out in the transfer market to build a squad that is capable of winning this season's Europa League. Whether the board have the same appetite to do that is another issue. Is it worth them spending big for the Europa League, when financial rewards aren't the same? The fans will certainly think so - and O'Neill might be the man to help give the hierarchy a nudge to help him, not just compete but be a force in the competition.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Wilson reports on Celtic's 5-1 AET defeat to Linz ASK, losing a four-goal lead to be knocked out of the Champions League

The fans are also hoping to see a considerable restructure at the club. Celtic still have board members involved in transfer negotiations and football operations. They got rid of their head of football Paul Tisdale in January and still haven't replaced him. There is still no head of recruitment, and they're still a number of first-team analysts short compared with the Brendan Rodgers era.

Celtic's hierarchy had seemed to be patching things up with the fans with their signings and a good domestic start to the season. Yesterday in Linz, chairman Brian Wilson sat and drank with the fans in the afternoon. A lot more patching up is required now.

Will Celtic ever get back to the Champions League?

If Celtic win the league this season, the task of reaching next season's Champions League is even harder. They will enter at the second qualifying round, meaning they will need to negotiate three ties and six matches to get into the league phase of the competition.

This was the last chance for a while that they just had a play-off to win, and it resulted in the sixth consecutive failure they've had in the qualifiers for this competition.

Celtic see themselves as a Champions League club - in stature and size they are. But it could be a while before their team plays in the tournament again.

One direct way into the tournament is by winning the Europa League…

Sports.title: Uefa poised to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
Sports.content:
Uefa is poised to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.

The Guardian understands European teams are likely to be cleared for participation in the upcoming under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.

Uefa had threatened the boycott after Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal was revealed and doubled down after it was withdrawn, saying the condition that “such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again” had not been met.

Quick Guide How do I 

Despite exchanging barbs in public, Uefa and Fifa are understood to have been having private discussions over the terms of removing the boycott threat for several weeks with the European governing body finally getting the reassurances it required.

When Fifa confirmed its decision to abandon FFE four days after it became public it neglected to pledge that a similar privatisation plan would not be repeated, but it has now done so in private correspondence.

A decision to drop the boycott will allow England, who named their squad for the under-20 tournament last week, to travel to Poland in time for the opening game against Canada on 5 September.

View image in fullscreen England’s under-20s are in line to go to the World Cup in Poland. Photograph: Carlos Rodrigues/The FA/Getty Images

France and Spain had also listed their travelling party in anticipation that the boycott would be lifted. Portugal, Italy and the host nation are the other European countries due to compete.

While the boycott is yet to be publicly dropped, it is among the topics that may arise in a meeting of Uefa’s executive committee and federation chiefs in Monte Carlo on Thursday. The 55 heads of Uefa’s member associations will convene before the Champions League draw during what is traditionally a significant few days in the European football calendar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Uefa’s position that Infantino must be replaced has not changed and further steps regarding its stance towards the Fifa leadership will also be discussed at the meeting on Thursday.

There will be relief in some quarters that younger players, in particular, will not become embroiled in the volatile battle for football’s future. But the fact that Fifa has been forced to mitigate for its president’s actions is another humiliation for a persistently scandal-hit organisation.

Sports.title: Martin O’Neill puts Champions League collapse among most painful Celtic nights
Sports.content:
Martin O’Neill has admitted that Celtic’s Champions League qualifying collapse from 4-0 up ranks as one of his most painful nights as the club’s manager.

Celtic held a four-goal aggregate lead against Lask on Tuesday when Callum McGregor scored in the 21st minute in Austria, building on a 3-0 first-leg victory, and appeared to be cruising into the league stage. But they lost 5-1 on the night after extra time to go out in extraordinary fashion.

Defeat sends Celtic into the Europa League and delivers a damaging financial blow that will cost the club at least £20m. O’Neill, who has overseen more than 300 games as the club’s manager, said the loss on Tuesday was one of the most painful.

“I would say absolutely, yes,” the 74-year-old said. “I’d put it down before the disappointment of losing the Uefa Cup final in 2003, but it’s so, so disappointing.

“We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal, which was great, we missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back. And obviously we conceded, from our viewpoint, not good goals at all. But that’s my team and that’s my responsibility.”

Asked whether his squad was strong enough, O’Neill said: “These are tough games. And it might only be a Champions League qualifying game, but it felt like a Champions League game. I thought they were a fine side. But that doesn’t matter. We should have been able to have seen it through. And we didn’t do. Talking about the squad, that’s for another day.”

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

McGregor, the captain, accepted there were no excuses. “We got what we deserved,” he told Amazon Prime. “I thought we were so passive. All night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game, and when you are 3-0 up it’s psychological.

“To be honest I didn’t think we were that good in the first leg, either. We scored at good times and kind of got away with it. You go 3-0 and you think you’ve got a real chance but when you play like that you can’t have any excuse whatsoever.

“We have to suck it up, apologise to the supporters and the club because there is no way that we should lose that game … Now you’ll see what kind of characters are in there.”

Sports.title: Manchester City confirm Bouaddi signing as Marmoush and González head out
Sports.content:
Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for €95m (£81.4m) plus €5m, with the 18-year-old midfielder agreeing a five-year contract.

Bouaddi’s arrival comes after City struck deals to loan Omar Marmoush to Tottenham for the season, with an obligation to buy for an initial £50m, and sell Nico González to Newcastle for £52m.

Bouaddi has experienced a rapid rise after becoming Lille’s youngest player when featuring against KÍ Klaksvík on 5 October 2023, three days after his 16th birthday. The Morocco international played 96 times for Lille and becomes the most expensive teenager signed by an English club.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I am happy with the progress I have made so far, but I also know I can improve so much,” Bouaddi said. “This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that. This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title.”

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, said: “Ayyoub’s potential is extremely high – a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs. At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo [Maresca].”

Bouaddi, who has played mainly as a No 6, continues City’s midfield rebuild. González is poised to become the fourth frontline central midfielder to depart this summer, after Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders. City have added Bouaddi and Elliott Anderson, a £116m buy from Nottingham Forest, and are expected to firm up their interest in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández by making a bid. The west London club value the midfielder at £120m.

View image in fullscreen Omar Marmoush is to sign a four-year contract with Spurs next summer when his loan ends. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images

Marmoush is to have a medical at Spurs, who have agreed to pay up to £10m in add-ons, with half of that guaranteed. Next summer the 27-year-old is to sign a four-year contract with a one-year option.

City are not due to give a sell-on fee to Eintracht Frankfurt, from whom they bought the Egyptian in January 2025. Marmoush is following Sávio in leaving City for Spurs, who bought the Brazilian winger in a deal worth £75m plus £10m on Tuesday. City have agreed a £34m fee for Palmeiras’s Allan Elias, who is to be Sávio’s replacement as a wide forward.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Spurs manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has been keen to bolster his options at centre-forward and Marmoush represents an upgrade on Dominic Solanke and Richarlison, who have struggled for consistency and fitness.

De Zerbi said at the end of July that Spurs had a “bomba” attacking signing lined up, meaning a top-tier player, and Marmoush and Sávio fit the bill. They have taken rather longer to join than he would have liked; he revealed on Tuesday that the negotiations for Sávio started three days after the end of last season. He believes they will be worth the wait.

Spurs have spent £304.5m this summer on Jan Paul van Hecke, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Sávio. They have added Martin Dubravka, Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers.

Sports.title: Bristol City ready to ‘supercharge growth’ and prove women’s clubs can fly solo
Sports.content:
As radiant, August sunshine glistens around a peacefully silent Ashton Gate before Bristol City Women’s pre-season media day, Hannah Buckley takes a seat, pitch side, with a gleam in her eye, surveying the scene. The sight of a top-class venue makes her beam in a way that perhaps only somebody whose CV includes job titles such as regional facilities manager and head of infrastructure, safety and sustainability can. Nice stadiums, particular ones used by women’s sports teams, give her a kick.

But after more than 20 years in football, the past eight at the WSL, Buckley is working on building something rather different: a club capable of thriving independently from the auspices of a men’s club. She was appointed as the Women’s Super League 2 side’s chief executive in May, starting her role in June, at a fascinating time in the team’s history, after they were taken over by the investment group Mercury13 last year to break away from the Bristol Sport group that oversees Bristol City’s men’s team and the city’s rugby union and basketball sides.

That breakaway has ensured it has been a relentlessly busy summer and Buckley, in her first sit-down interview, explains some of their changes: “Our headcount in staff has doubled. We’re having to put in place all the back-house services, which historically would have been carried by Bristol Sport. We’ve made improvements at the training ground, we have upgraded our training pitch, and I think I’d describe it as: ‘We’re in the marginal gain phase,’ reviewing what we have to do [to] supercharge our growth and success.”

Buckley, a board member at Somerset County Cricket Club, remembers the anguish she felt when told girls could not play football at her school when she was 11. She revived her playing days at university but creating opportunities for young girls is partly why she says it was a “no-brainer to apply” for the CEO role at Bristol City. There is a vast catchment area for youngsters across the south-west and she says: “It’s a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. It’s a true ‘build’ project.”

View image in fullscreen Hannah Buckley, Bristol City Women’s chief executive, says: ‘We are technically nine months old as a business.’ Photograph: BCWFC

Mercury13, which has investment from familiar names such as the former Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata, owns three women’s clubs: FC Como Women in Italy, FC Badalona Women in Spain and Bristol City Women. Their standalone focus on women’s football, without ties to a men’s team, excites Buckley, who recently led the WSL’s design guidelines for building or upgrading venues specifically for women’s teams. She says: “Independent clubs don’t carry some of the risks that you potentially see where the men’s club may get relegated or [have a] change in ownership and so the independent nature of the club for me was a real opportunity.

“What’s really interesting for me with being part of a multi-club ownership group dedicated solely to women’s football is the opportunities for research, the opportunities for cross-collaboration with different sporting competitions, and actually demonstrating that you can make it work as a standalone women’s entity.”

The owners’ passion specifically for women’s football has also invigorated City’s head coach, Charlotte Healy, who took over in June 2025 after coaching at clubs including Manchester United, Manchester City, Liverpool, Chesterfield and Derby. Healy says: “This football club, I really feel like it cares about its women’s team.

“We had to evolve the workforce – when I came in, I think there was probably [only] seven or eight staff – but we’re already starting to see that the people we’ve brought in the building are good people and we’re really starting to see the benefit of their expertise.

“[For example] we’ve brought a performance wellbeing manager in, which I think was really important – helping the players, because being a professional footballer is not easy, to come in and play under pressure environments and have to win. We brought in a head of performance services in January, who [has] great WSL experience – because we can talk about ‘being WSL ready’, but if we’ve got staff who don’t know what WSL ready looks like, how are we going to get there?”

Buckley adds to that list of hires by saying: “We now have a commercial director and a head of finance, we now have a full-time marketing manager, a club secretary.” And then there have been the most important recruits: players.

They include the 20-year-old Australia defender Alexia Apostolakis, who signed from Melbourne City in July and says part of the reason she moved from the other side of the world was “how ambitious Charlotte and the staff were to get promoted”. Healy says of the summer recruitment: “We felt we needed more squad depth, and I think we’ve made some really good signings. We’ve again looked at younger players. Alexia is one of the best young players in Australia.”

View image in fullscreen The defender Alexia Apostolakis, a summer signing, is described as ‘one of the best young players in Australia’. Photograph: Ali Painter/WSL/Getty Images

The Finland forward Lotta Lindström, who signed from London City Lionesses, says Healy’s team having been the top scorers in WSL2 last term was part of the attraction. The 21-year-old has for two years running been in squads that have won the division, with London City in 2023-24, then on loan at Birmingham City last season, and she says: “I hope I can bring up that winning mentality and [help by] doing those little things right, those little things that actually make the difference between being good and being the best.”

Healy is not shy about stating their goal, as they try to improve on last season’s fourth place. Last term, the top two were promoted, with the third-place team going up after a playoff against the WSL’s bottom side. This time, there will be one automatic spot and the sides in second and third will battle for a place in a playoff against the second-bottom WSL side. Healy believes defensive improvements can help them take the next step: “We want this club to be in the WSL. We understand the challenges that come with that – every team wants to be in the WSL. We need to be a little bit more consistent. We scored the most goals in the league last year and finished fourth, so it is really clear that we needed to be better out of possession. Our biggest evolution needs to be without the ball and making sure that we concede fewer goals – if we can do that, we’ll be right up at the top.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Buckley, who was part of the Football Association facilities team that developed St George’s Park into the national football centre and therefore is perhaps accustomed to a patient approach, says rather more cautiously: “I would say it [WSL2] is the hardest league to get promoted from – you only have to slip up once or twice and the opportunity goes. You saw how tight the margins were last year.

“There are so many facets to success – building the right culture here, first and foremost, is the important thing, professionalising our environment and setting ourselves up for success. I’d hope that we achieve top three. I think that would be a fantastic outcome. But I also have to be really measured; we are technically nine months old as a business.”

She points to their opening fixtures – away to Sunderland, another side taken over by a multi-club women’s-focused ownership group, the Bay Collective, then at Ashton Gate against promotion-chasing Newcastle – as a good “barometer check”, before concluding: “Ask me again at Christmas!”

Robins tend to thrive at Christmas. Whatever their final position, this could be an intriguing case study to observe how well women’s teams can fly solo.

Sports.title: Forest in talks with Celta Vigo over Javi Rueda as Axel Disasi joins Palace on loan
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest are in talks over the €15m (£12.8m) signing of the Celta Vigo right-back Javi Rueda, which would probably be their final incoming of the window after Liam Delap from Chelsea.

Oliver Glasner has been seeking someone who can play right wing-back and the 24-year-old former Real Madrid academy player fits the desired profile.

The former Spain youth international joined Celta three years ago from Madrid, who will receive half the fee. He made his first-team breakthrough last season, playing 26 La Liga games and 11 in the Europa League, helping his side to reach the quarter-finals.

Forest confirmed on Wednesday that the wing-back Eric da Silva Moreira will spend the season on loan to the Dutch side Excelsior to aid his development.

Chelsea have agreed to sell Delap to Forest in a deal worth £50m and have loaned Axel Disasi to Crystal Palace for the season. Disasi has also been borrowed by Aston Villa and West Ham since he signed for Chelsea from Monaco.

The defender said: “I know that it’s very tough to play against Palace at Selhurst Park – so I’m looking forward to being on the other side now.”

Brentford have struck an agreement with West Ham to sign El Hadji Malick Diouf for £35m plus up to £5m in add-ons. The left-back has been keen to leave West Ham since their relegation.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession
Sports.content:
The former England forward Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway, police have said.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May. The 31-year-old is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported. Sterling, from Berkshire, is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court for a hearing on 15 September.

Quick Guide How do I 

He scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side to reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the Euro 2020 final. Sterling came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut and moved in 2015 to Manchester City, with whom he won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup.

Sterling left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour he spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal. After leaving Stamford Bridge, he joined the Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of last season. He is now without a club.

In the 2021 Queen’s birthday honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 5: Charlton Athletic
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 14th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd (WSL2)

Prospects

Just under 20 years since Charlton’s successful women’s team were disbanded after the men’s team’s relegation from the Premier League, they are finally back in the limelight and ready to make a name for themselves again.

Karen Hills’s side impressed for much of last season, going on a 27-game unbeaten streak and possessing the meanest defence in WSL 2. A mid-season blip harmed their race for the title, however, and they lost out to Birmingham City on the final day of the season, ultimately going through a playoff to achieve their goal of promotion. Beating Leicester in that game will have given Hills and her players confidence that they can compete. There will be no complacency, however, having seen how newly promoted sides have fared in recent history.

Six players have departed since last season, including the influential Katie Bradley But they have been replaced with a blend of knowhow and exciting young talent. The arrival of Ashleigh Neville and Emily van Egmond will bring experience to Hills’s dressing room. Leah Davidson’s and Grace Johnston’s arrivals from Australia are intriguing moves. Meanwhile, Sophie Whitehouse was the hero of the previous campaign and Charlton will be looking to the goalkeeper to again lead from the back. It is the attacking side of the game that perhaps causes the most concern. Charlton managed only 31 goals last season, the lowest of the WSL2’s top six.

Preparations got under way with a pre-season trip to Cádiz, a chance for a new-look side to come together. There is no doubt that the task to stay up is a challenging one, but a club that have defied the odds on more than one occasion will believe they can do it again.

Off-field picture

A record-breaking partnership has seen haircare brand Sofnfree become the women’s team’s official sleeve partner. The branding will feature on all playing and replica shirts this season, while content creation will be a focus as Charlton hope to access new and existing audiences. The club have also launched their first women’s-centric TikTok channel. The news, however, that ownership group Global Football Partners have put the club up for sale could cause a bit of instability in the short term.

The manager

Reaching the Women’s Super League was part of the five-year plan Hills had when she was appointed in 2021, bringing a club close to her heart back into the limelight. The 51-year-old represented Chartlon for six years as a player, winning the FA Cup in 2005. This is the second time in Hills’s coaching career she has guided a team to the top flight, having previously done so with Tottenham in 2019, and watching Charlton walk out at the Valley against Liverpool on 6 September will inevitably be an emotional moment for her.

View image in fullscreen Karen Hills has guided a club into the top flight for the second time after have done so with Spurs in 2019. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Alamy

Star signing

Only three months ago, Neville was lining up against Charlton in the promotion playoff. Now she is a fully fledged Addick, joining from Leicester on a two-year deal. The full-back brings with her a wealth of experience having made more than a century of appearances in the WSL. The majority of those were under Hills at Tottenham after arriving there from Coventry United. A tough-tackling, intuitive defender, Neville never shirks a challenge and has the ability to push forward. She will also be a strong leader in the dressing room.

Stat attack

Despite finishing third in WSL2, Charlton kept the joint-most clean sheets and conceded the fewest goals in the division. No club saved as high a percentage of their shots on target faced, with Whitehouse playing every minute. She saved four penalties in the playoff shootout, too.

Set for a breakthrough

Johnston was named Charlton’s first signing of the summer during a transfer window that has seen many A-League players depart for Europe. The versatile young full-back arrives at the Valley hoping to make her mark on English football after three seasons with Perth Glory. She impressed during her time with her home town club, played every minute of last season, winning the club’s 2026 best young player award. Johnston’s form led to her being called up to the Young Matildas in 2023, representing the under-20s and now the under-23s. She was an integral member of the squad that won the Asean Women’s Championship last year.

What they say …

“I know what Karen’s about and vice versa; she knows what I bring. I’m really looking forward to working with her again” – Ashleigh Neville

Where are they playing their home games?

Charlton will play their home games at the Valley for a third consecutive season. Season-ticket sales started almost immediately after their successful promotion push. Alcohol will also still be allowed in the stadium, with an alcohol-free section established. Other fan activations include giving supporters the opportunity to sponsor a player.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jean-Philippe Mateta to Aston Villa?
Sports.content:
Liam Delap may not have broken any records during his time with Chelsea but he is setting one on his way out the door. The England youth international is thought to be breaking Nottingham Forest’s transfer fee record with Oliver Glasner bringing him in for an expected £50m. The fee comes despite a disappointing 2025-26 season with the 23-year-old striker scoring only one Premier League goal.

Injury problems with his shoulder and hamstring did not help but the lack of return means the Blues were open to selling the striker and Forest have taken the bait. If Delap does sell for £50m it also means Chelsea will make a £20m profit on the player after buying him from Ipswich for £30m in 2025.

Delap isn’t the last deal Forest want to get over the line before Monday’s deadline day either as they are interested in Corinthians and Brazil midfielder André.

One story that is gathering momentum like a ball in snow is Jean-Philippe Mateta moving to Aston Villa. The Villans have made Crystal Palace an offer for the France striker but it is a long way off what the London club would like.

A departure that could finance Mateta’s move could be that of Ollie Watkins, though it is one that has shocked Villa. It has been extensively reported the English international has interest from Saudi club Al-Hilal with his signature set to be worth about £59.8m. Villa are close to agreeing the move and it is understood Watkins would have an annual salary of £12m.

With deadline day approaching, last-minute signings will come out of the woodwork at every turn. Let’s rattle through some. Manchester United are interested in Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, Newcastle have submitted a bid for Lille winger Matias Fernandez-Pardo, West Ham defender El Hadji Malick Diouf may play in the Premier League again with Brentford close to a deal for the Senegalese player, newly promoted Hull have agreed a move to sign Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin in a deal worth £20m and Tottenham are pushing to sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.

If Spurs did get that move over the line for the Egypt forward then the club’s spend this summer would be close to £400m. It is no wonder fans looked lost for words at Tottenham’s 3-0 loss to Brentford last weekend.

We started with Chelsea so let’s end with the Blues. Enzo Fernández, who was met with a wall of boos when Chelsea played Fulham in their opening fixture, may not play in London for much longer. Manchester City will submit a bid for the Argentina midfielder before deadline day. If they do, it could be the biggest transfer of the summer so far with Chelsea reportedly wanting £120m for the 25-year-old.

So Fernández may travel up the M1 and M6 but the boos are likely to follow him after he scored and showboated in England’s defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

Sports.title: Chelsea offered Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa - who Juventus bid just £6m for - to fix their goalkeeper problem after Robert Sanchez shocker
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their want-away goalkeeper.

After his move to Juventus collapsed earlier this month despite an initial £6million offer, Martinez is now one of three senior keepers in the Villa squad following the arrival of Zion Suzuki at Villa Park.

Martinez is also Villa's top earner following the departure of Youri Tielemans to Manchester United in July, and Unai Emery intends to press ahead with Suzuki and Marco Bizot.

Earlier in the summer, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso indicated he was happy with keepers Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders.

But Sanchez's shaky display in Chelsea's 3-2 win at Fulham raised more question marks about the Spaniard.

Aston Villa have replaced Emiliano Martinez with Zion Suzuki and he is available for transfer

Asked about Sanchez on Wednesday, Alonso said: 'Normal conversations. We have talked more about the team thing, about what we did well and what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context.

'Every game is going to be important because we are in this process that we still need to develop things, we need to make adjustments that are more team-related.'

Chelsea have brought 21-year-old Belgian Mike Penders into their squad after a successful loan at Strasbourg last season.

Alonso today suggested he is likely to start Thursday's Carabao Cup game against Luton Town. 'He's in the squad and will have an opportunity,' he said.

The Blues rate the former Genk youth shot-stopper, who has been likened to former Chelsea man Thibaut Courtois, very highly.

A move for Martinez, at 33 years old, would not be viewed as blocking Penders' progress.

Sports.title: Brentford get their £35m man from West Ham, Villa expect Al Hilal to pay £50m asking price for Watkins, Liverpool explore other options with Brighton wanting £80m for Minteh and all options remain open for Grealish: WINDOW WATCH

Martinez offered to Chelsea

Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their wantaway goalkeeper.

Man City complete ins and outs as they wait to go back in for Enzo

City have confirmed the £85.6m signing of 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. The Morocco midfielder said: 'Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world.

'I’ve watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football and they have shown they are winners – this club feels like it’s built to win. The squad is world class and Enzo (Maresca) is a top manager.'

Ayyoub Bouaddi has joined Manchester City in a £85.6m deal from Lille

Aston Villa expect Saudis to meet £50m Watkins asking price

Aston Villa expect Al Hilal to hit their valuation of £50million for Ollie Watkins if they complete a deal for the England forward.

Jack Grealish is now back at Manchester City but all options are open as the window closes

The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but Corinthians are holding out for more.

Javi Rueda (left) in action in Celta Vigo's La Liga opener against Valencia at the weekend

Palacios set for £23.5m Ipswich deal

Ipswich are finalising a £23.5m deal for Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios. The 27-year-old has agreed a four-year contract. As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Ipswich want £9m for midfielder Anis Mehmeti, who has offers from Wrexham, Birmingham and Derby.

Ezequiel Palacios is set to became the latest signing in a busy summer at Portman Road

We've still got a lot to replace and now Milly is another one we've got to replace.'

Sports.title: Fears as police launch search for ex-Premier League star who has been missing in Hungary for over a week
Sports.content:
Police in Hungary have launched a search for former Premier League star Akos Buzsaky, who has been missing for more than a week.

The 44-year-old, who played for QPR in the English top flight, has been missing from Budapest since August 18.

The midfielder earned 20 caps for Hungary as a midfielder and also played for Plymouth, Portsmouth and Barnsley before retiring in 2025. He made 18 Premier League appearances, contributing two goals and two assists.

The police have not said why they are looking for Buzsaky and his father, Akos Buzsaky Sr told Hungarian outlet Blikk: ‘I didn’t know that the police were also looking for my son.

Akos Buszaky played for QPR between 2007 and 2012, with one season in the top flight

Sports.title: Champions League draw's BANNED matches: Why Liverpool vs Real Madrid and Inter Milan vs Arsenal will be outlawed in first year of new UEFA rules
Sports.content:
Champions League draw's BANNED matches: Why Liverpool vs Real Madrid and Inter Milan vs Arsenal will be outlawed in first year of new UEFA rules

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool vs Real Madrid and Inter Milan vs Arsenal will not be allowed in this season's Champions League league phase due a little-known new rule introduced by UEFA.

The draw for the competition takes place tomorrow, with each team to face two sides from Pot 1, Pot 2, Pot 3 and Pot 4.

Liverpool, Real, Inter and Arsenal are all in Pot 1, and therefore in principle the Reds could be drawn against the Spanish giants at Anfield, and Inter could host the Gunners at the San Siro.

However, UEFA rules prevent this from happening because of recent history.

Liverpool have faced Real at home in the past two seasons, while Inter have also entertained Arsenal twice in the league phase over the same timeframe.

And, the European governing body have now brought in a ruling that is based around stopping the same fixture happening three years in a row.

Liverpool won't be able to draw Real Madrid at home in this season's Champions League league phase after UEFA introduced a new rule

The rule also applies to Inter Milan hosting Arsenal after the fixture took place in the last two years

A section of the Champions League regulations says: 'UEFA administration may determine alternative conditions for the draw in accordance with the principles set by the Club Competitions Committee and may adapt any of the conditions of the draw to avoid deadlock situations and/or take into account any relevant constraints in light of decisions taken by the UEFA Executive Committee.'

They added: 'The UEFA Club Competitions Committee has determined an additional condition that may be applicable to the UEFA Champions League draw for the 2026-27 season, deciding that any individual fixture between the same two teams may not be repeated in the same competition with the same home team for three consecutive seasons.

'This means that if any teams that already played against each other in the league phase of the UEFA Champions League in the 2024-25 season are again drawn against each other, with the same home team, in the league phase of the UEFA Champions League in this 2025-26 season, those teams will not be able to be drawn against each other with the same home team in the 2026-27 season.'

This does mean that the teams can be drawn against each other, but this would have to be with the match between Liverpool and Real at the Bernabeu, and at the Emirates for Inter vs Arsenal.

A fixture between Real and Liverpool would have plenty of spice due to their recent history, coupled with the fact that former Liverpool stars Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konate now play for the Spanish giants.

Both teams endured a disappointing time in Europe last season as they exited at the quarter-final stage.

Liverpool were beaten 4-0 on aggregate by eventual winners PSG, while Real lost 6-4 to Bayern Munich over two legs.

Meanwhile, Inter were shocked by Bodo/Glimt at the play-off stage, while Arsenal lost the final to PSG on penalties.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo is hauled off, mid-tantrum, at half-time by no-nonsense Ange Postecoglou - before team turn a 2-0 deficit into 3-2 win without him - in new challenge to his Saudi supremacy
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo's relationship with new Al Nassr boss Ange Postecoglou already appears to be under scrutiny just three matches into the season.

Al Nassr completed a remarkable comeback from two goals down to beat rivals Al Ettifaq 3-2 on Tuesday, but it was no thanks to Ronaldo, who earns an astronomical £488,000 a day, that the reigning champions claimed all three points.

The visitors appeared to be heading for defeat after enduring a disastrous first half which saw goalkeeper Bento sent off in the 12th minute for a challenge on former Fulham midfielder Mousa Dembele after rushing out of his box.

Al Ettifaq capitalised, with Ondrej Duda and Alvaro Medran finding the back of the net to take a two-goal lead into half-time.

Ronaldo, who was making his first start of the season following his return from the summer's World Cup, cut a frustrated figure as he headed towards the dressing room at the break.

The 41-year-old forward was seen angrily gesturing and removing his captain's armband as he walked down the tunnel.

Postecoglou then boldly opted to remove Ronaldo before the start of the second half in what turned out to be an inspired move.

Ronaldo couldn't help but hide his frustration after enduring a disastrous first half which saw the reigning champions trail by two goals and reduced to 10 men

He was seen angrily gesturing and removing his captain's armband as he walked down the tunnel at half-time

Postecoglou then boldly opted to remove Ronaldo before the start of the second half in what turned out to be an inspired move

Sadio Mane sparked the revival in the 74th minute before defender Abdulelah Al Amri levelled the match three minutes later. Mane then found the back of the net again in the 90th minute to complete the turnaround and seal victory.

Footage of the post-match celebrations showed no sign of Ronaldo celebrating the victory, while Postecoglou refused to indulge questions about his controversial call to drop the Portugal star after the match.

'I think there’s a bigger story today, and that is that ten men of Al Nassr were unbelievable. That's all you should write about today, everything else doesn't matter.

'It doesn't matter what team because if you see ten men in those conditions for so long, 2-0 down to come back, that's the only story today.'

Controversy appears to have followed Ronaldo since his move to the Middle East in January 2023, following his public fallout with Manchester United.

At the beginning of the year Ronaldo went on strike over what he felt was a lack of financial backing of his Al Nassr compared to their title rivals Al Hilal. Both clubs are majority owned by The Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund.

Ronaldo was convinced that Al Hilal are getting preferential treatment, and he was particularly angry that they strengthened their squad by bringing in players such as his former Real Madrid teammate Karim Benzema during the January window.

Saudi officials, meanwhile, were surprised that Ronaldo was unhappy given he is earning nearly £500,000 a day.

Footage of the post-match celebrations showed no sign of Ronaldo celebrating the victory

Ange Postecoglou:



“I think there’s a bigger story today, and that’s that the ten Al Nassr players put in an incredible performance. That’s all you should be writing about today.”

pic.twitter.com/7jSMfBAtqp — Al Nassr Zone (@TheNassrZone) August 26, 2026

Although Ronaldo is the face of the Saudi Pro League (SPL), the league issued a statement firing back at the Portuguese star by reaffirming that he has no say on what happens at clubs outside of his own.

'The SPL is structured around a simple principle: every club operates independently under the same rules,' they said.

'Clubs have their own boards, their own executives and their own football leadership. Decisions on recruitment, spending and strategy sit with those clubs, within a financial framework designed to ensure sustainability and competitive balance. That framework applies equally across the league.

'Cristiano has been fully engaged with Al Nassr since his arrival and has played an important role in the club's growth and ambition. Like any elite competitor, he wants to win. But no individual - however significant - determines decisions beyond their own club.'

Ronaldo claimed his first league title with Al Nassr last season.

Sports.title: Newcastle Confidential: Why Matias Fernandez-Pardo deal is NOT dead, Joelinton injury REVEALED, what William Osula absence means for Yoane Wissa and the Yankuba Minteh sell-on clause
Sports.content:
Newcastle have NOT given up hope of signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.

There were reports in France today of the Magpies walking away from a deal amid Lille’s £60m asking price. Newcastle Confidential understands that is not yet the case, although sporting director Ross Wilson will not sanction any deal that leads to future problems with Premier League and UEFA spending rules. Wilson and the hierarchy have solved those issues this summer and there is now a transfer framework within which they are operating.

Fernandez-Pardo is an ambitious target and the club’s interest was revealed in the final Confidential column of last season. It was thought then that the 21-year-old wanted Champions League football, but there has been encouragement in recent days of him being open to the move.

The £50million marquee signing of Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City has been a huge boost in terms of the optics around a club who have lost several stars this summer.

This comes on the back of confirmation of plans for a new £190million training ground development and the impressive showing in the season opener against Liverpool. There is a feeling inside St James' Park, and among the fanbase, of renewed positivity heading out of the summer.

Fernandez-Pardo, a Belgium international, is seen as a versatile forward who can play in any of the four attacking positions used by new boss Matthias Jaissle.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is an ambitious target and Newcastle's interest was revealed in the final Confidential column of last season

Joelinton injury boost

Joelinton has a quad injury but the problem is not as serious as first feared, Confidential can reveal.

Mystery has surrounded the nature of the Brazilian’s issue since Jaissle told reporters 11 days ago that he would miss at least a ‘couple of weeks’ with an unspecified injury.

We now understand there were concerns that Joelinton could be set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines. He needed surgery on his thigh in 2024 and missed four months of the season. However, the 30-year-old does not require an operation this time and the news has been more positive in recent days. Indeed, once the symptoms subside, he will be free to return.

That exact date is still to be determined, but it is hoped that will be this side of the September international break.

Newcastle's Joelinton has a quad injury - but it is not as bad as first feared

Toon set for slice of Minteh fee

Newcastle DO have a sell-on clause in the deal that took Yankuba Minteh to Brighton two years ago.

Liverpool want to sign the 22-year-old and are willing to pay £65million to take him to Anfield. The Seagulls are holding out for closer to £80million and negotiations are ongoing.

Minteh joined Brighton for £30million from Newcastle in the summer of 2024 as the club scrambled to avoid a Premier League points deduction for breaching profit and sustainability rules. But we can reveal that, unlike the deal that took Elliot Anderson to Nottingham Forest on the same weekend, the package with Brighton does include a sell-on clause.

The value of this is thought to be around 10 per cent of the profit of any sale, meaning the Magpies could be set for a return of £4-5million should the winger move to Liverpool, a not-insignificant sum in a world of Squad Cost Ratio rules.

Yankuba Minteh could be heading for Liverpool from Brighton - which would land Newcastle a cut of the fee

No surgery for Burn

Dan Burn has damaged the deltoid ligaments in his ankle and is likely to be missing until mid-October, Confidential understands.

The good news is that the club captain does not need surgery and there is still an outside chance that he could return just before the September break. However, Burn will not be rushed and the expectation is that he will use that three-week period for international matches to build his fitness on Tyneside.

The protective boot he is wearing has given rise to fears of the problem being more serious, but that is standard practice for such an injury.

The deltoid ligament is a strong, triangle-shaped band of connective tissue on the inside of the ankle that stabilises the area and prevents outward rolling of the foot. Burn damaged his deltoid ligaments when his foot rolled in training last week.

Newcastle will not, as it stands, enter the market for a new centre-back. Sven Botman answered some of the concerns around him from pre-season with a strong display against Liverpool on Sunday.

Dan Burn in his protective boot on Sunday - but the good news is he won't require an operation

Osula blow a real pain

Finally, on injuries at least, William Osula has avoided a broken foot but will face a spell on the sidelines.

We understand the striker suffered the injury when he collided with Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson during the first half of Sunday’s 2-2 draw. Osula played on before succumbing to the pain 10 minutes after half-time.

While there is no significant damage, it looks like being an absence that is measured in weeks rather than days, with the pain needing to settle before a return date is set.

That is a blow given Osula was lively and helped set the tone against the Reds. It is likely that Yoane Wissa will revert to striker as opposed to Nick Woltemade, with Jacob Ramsey and Joe Willock vying for the No10 role at Tottenham on Saturday.

Woltemade’s future is uncertain and there could yet be movement in the final days of the window should an offer emerge, most likely from Germany.

Willock is wanted by Besiktas and Newcastle have a decision to make with the midfielder in the final year on his contract. Jaissle told us on Sunday that he wants to keep him.

William Osula was superb for Newcastle on Sunday and his injury is a real blow for Matthias Jaissle

Pope to stay

Nick Pope will be staying at Newcastle beyond the transfer window, as it stands.

We are told that the goalkeeping slots at viable suitors are all taken at this present time and, barring injury to those keepers or an unexpected approach over the weekend, the 34-year-old will remain at St James’ Park entering the final year of his contract.

Newcastle are still trying to find a solution given Pope has been told he would be third choice, but time is running out.

Toon kids shining

I went to watch the Under 21s on Monday night during their 3-1 defeat by Tottenham.

We should expect to see striker Sean Neave and defender Miodrag Pivas involved in tonight’s Carabao Cup tie against West Brom after they were taken off at half-time at Whitley Park, but Mason Miley played the full match.

Of those who caught the eye, Korean winger Park Seung-Soo was the pick, while scorer Vakhtang Salia clearly has ability.

I know those on the inside are excited about the 18-year-old Georgian, whose first year on Tyneside was disrupted by injury. He looks like a forward with scope for big improvement.
